title: FDF: replies and review status keep their parent comment (fixes #333)
author: SBaksa
body:
Fixes #333.

## What was wrong

FDF export removed `/IRT` from every comment, because it is a reference into the source document and would dangle in the FDF. Nothing replaced it. A note's replies and its review-status reply (`/State (Accepted)`, `/StateModel (Review)`) therefore imported as unrelated top-level comments. XFDF was not affected: it writes `inreplyto="<parent NM>"` and relinks it on import.

## Fix (`crates/xfdf`)

- **Export:** each comment is now an indirect object of the FDF (objects 2, 3, …, listed in `/Annots`), and a reply's `/IRT` points at its parent's object in the FDF, as ISO 32000-2 §12.7.8.3.1 allows. The FDF now carries a cross-reference table. A reply whose parent isn't exported is written without `/IRT`, as before.
- **Import:** comments are placed first, then replies are linked in a second pass, the same approach as the XFDF import. If the parent isn't in the FDF, the import falls back to a comment with the parent's `/NM` already in the document. `/IRT` is no longer passed through `deep()`, which would otherwise have copied the parent comment inline.
- FDFs with direct comment dictionaries and no `/IRT` (older PdfCraft exports and other producers) import unchanged.

## Tests

- `fdf_keeps_replies_and_review_status_on_their_note`: the scenario from #333 (a note on page 2, two replies, Accepted status). After export and import, each reply's parent and the review state match the source. Re-importing the same file keeps the thread. Every cross-reference offset points at its object.
- `fdf_round_trips_values_and_comments` now also asserts that the comment view (including `reply_to`) matches the source.

title: M3: render pool renders each request once when the caller re-sends it
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

The canvas rebuilds its render queue every frame from what it is still missing (page rasters, tiles, text layers, thumbnails), and calls `RenderPool::set_queue` whenever that list changes, which happens whenever any answer arrives. A request a worker has already popped is still missing until its answer arrives, so each re-send put it back in the queue, and the next idle worker rendered it a second time.

- With one worker, every other page was rendered twice. While page 1 renders, page 2 is popped; page 1's answer triggers a re-send that still lists page 2.
- With 7 workers (the default on an 8-core machine), about half of all renders were duplicates.
- A slow page (dense vector drawing) was taken by worker after worker until the 20 s watchdog fired. The `stuck` set only stops that after the watchdog, so for those 20 s a single complex page could hold several workers.

## Fix

`crates/render/src/raster.rs` only. There is no API change and no new dependency.

- The pool remembers the requests its workers have **taken** until `try_recv` hands out their answer (`Shared::taken`).
- A worker pops the most urgent queued request that isn't already taken (`take_next`, under the queue lock, so two workers can't take the same request).
- When `try_recv` hands out an answer, it removes queued copies of that request. That closes the gap between "answered" and the caller's next `set_queue`.
- Watchdog answers and panic answers go through `try_recv` like any other answer, so they clear `taken` too.

**Why nothing visible changes:** a pool's bytes and settings are fixed for its lifetime (the engine builds a new pool after every edit, layer change or comment-visibility change). Equal requests to one pool therefore always produce the same answer. Callers get exactly one answer per request instead of one or more identical ones, sooner. Pixels are untouched. Rendering itself isn't modified, and the inline (web) pool path is unchanged.

## Measurements

These come from a lo…

title: M1: incremental saves are allocated once at their exact size
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

`write_incremental` copied the original file into a buffer of `original.len() + 4096` bytes, then appended the revision. When the revision is larger than 4 KB the buffer grows. `Vec` doubles its capacity when it grows, so it reallocates at twice the size:

- the whole original is copied a **second** time;
- the result keeps up to the **original's size again** as unused capacity.

The engine keeps that result as the document's working bytes. Those bytes go to the render pool, to `save_bytes`, and, after `mark_saved`, become the base of every later edit. So the unused half stays alive as long as the document is open.

Revisions over 4 KB are ordinary: rotating a few dozen pages, an image, a batch of comments.

## Fix

`crates/cos/src/writer.rs` only:

- The revision is written into its own buffer, with offsets counted from `base` (the original's length, plus the newline added when the original doesn't end in one).
- The result is then allocated once, at exactly `original + revision`, and filled in one pass.
- `write_xref_stream` takes that `base`. `write_full` passes `0`, so full saves are unchanged.

**The output is byte for byte what it was before.** Nothing else changes: no API, no file format, no behaviour.

## Evidence

**Byte-identical output.** A local harness (not committed) applied a fixed set of edits to several originals and hashed what `write_incremental` returned, before and after the change. The edits were: a `/Info` change, a new integer, a new stream of 10 B, 3 KB, 5 KB or 200 KB, and an added-then-freed object. The originals were:

- the classic cross-reference table fixture;
- the same file saved with an xref stream;
- the fixture with no final newline;
- the fixture encrypted with AES-256;

title: M7: Arabic in added text (shaping, bidi order, searchable Type 3 glyphs)
author: fares111111122
body:
Add text used to write Arabic as `?` (standard-14 fonts, WinAnsi). Items with Arabic are now shaped and laid out correctly, and stay searchable.

Refs #250, #280, #369. This covers **writing** Arabic with Add text; the other parts of those issues (RTL typing in the box, editing existing Arabic text, system fonts) stay open.

## How it works
- **Shaping** (`pdfcraft-fonts`, new `arabic.rs`): the craft-fonts `Arab` face (Noto Sans Arabic) through `harfrust`, which is already in the tree via egui and uses the same `read-fonts` as `skrifa`. It handles joining forms, ligatures and mark positions. Output is clusters (a letter with its dots or marks) in drawing order.

Arabic and its neutrals go to the Arabic face, which mirrors brackets. Latin text and digits keep the item's standard font. Justified right-to-left paragraphs end at the right edge.
- **PDF output**: each distinct cluster is one glyph of a Type 3 font drawn from the face's outlines (the same approach as the Japanese fallback in `text.rs`), with a ToUnicode entry. No font file is embedded. `text_extract`, copy and search get every letter exactly once; one glyph per cluster keeps a letter's dots from leaking into the text.
- **Font names**: fonts are named so they are free on the page. A full save renumbers objects but not resource names, so object numbers alone could collide. Updating or deleting an item removes its fonts. Outlines are read before anything is written, so a failure leaves the document unchanged.

title: M3: rendered pixels are moved out of the pixmap, not copied
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

Every page, tile and thumbnail raster was copied once more than needed. `render_page` ended with

```rust
Ok((pixmap.width() as u32, pixmap.height() as u32, pixmap.data_as_u8_slice().to_vec(), None))
```

That allocates a second buffer the size of the raster and copies every pixel into it, while the pixmap's own buffer is still alive. A full page can be up to `MAX_PIXELS` (64 MP, 256 MB of RGBA). For as long as the copy runs, each worker needs twice the raster's memory, and with up to 7 workers that adds up during zooming.

## Fix

`crates/render/src/raster.rs`: the bytes are moved out of the pixmap instead of copied.

```rust
fn into_bytes(pixmap: Pixmap) -> Vec<u8> {
    bytemuck::allocation::try_cast_vec(pixmap.take()).unwrap_or_else(|(_, pixels)| pixels.iter().flat_map(|p| [p.r, p.g, p.b, p.a]).collect())
}
```

- `Pixmap::take` hands over vello_cpu's `Vec<PremulRgba8>`. Each pixel is four one-byte channels in RGBA order, the same bytes `data_as_u8_slice` exposes, and `try_cast_vec` reinterprets the vector as bytes in place.
- The cast cannot fail from 4-byte, 1-aligned pixels to bytes (same alignment, sizes divide). The fallback copy exists only because the signature returns a `Result`. It has no panic path.
- `bytemuck` becomes a direct dependency of `pdfcraft-render`, with `extern_crate_alloc`. It is already in the tree through hayro and vello, so `Cargo.lock` gains one line and no new package.

`RenderedPage`, the pool and every caller are unchanged.

## Evidence

**Pixels are identical.** A local harness (not committed) rendered every page of #260's `pdf_engine_test.pdf` at scale 1, at scale 2.5, and as a 512×512 tile at scale 3, then hashed the RGBA. All 33 hashes are the same on `main` and on this branch.

**Memory and time.** One 6182×8000 px page (197 MB of RGBA, 2,000 filled rectangles) rendered with `PageRenderer`, three runs each, release build on an Apple M1 Pro:

| | Peak RSS (`/usr/bin/time -l`) | Render time |

title: Never crash: dash patterns can't exhaust memory or hang the renderer
author: jcl-bit
body:
Found by `cargo xtask fuzz` (4 jobs, 300 s, Windows, seeded from the pinned pdf.js corpus). The finding was a 392-byte page whose ExtGState dashes a line that starts far off the page. Triage found the same class in ordinary-looking pages, and a hang right next to it:

| Input | Where | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| ExtGState `/D [[11] 0]` on a line from x = 92234775807 (the fuzz finding) | `hayro` stroke expansion: kurbo keeps every dash | over 5 GB, killed | 0.2 s, a few MB |
| `[0.000001] 0 d` on an ordinary 20 pt line | same | over 10 GB in 1.6 s | 0.2 s, a few MB |
| `[1] 0 d` under a `cm` that shrinks by 10^7 | same | over 10 GB | 0.2 s |
| a long pattern on many short subpaths (kurbo restarts the pattern at every `m` and `h`) | same | runs out of memory | 0.2 s |
| `[-1 -1] 0 d` (entries summing to less than zero) | kurbo's search for the starting dash | **never finishes** (killed after 120 s, flat memory) | 0.2 s |

On the desktop the render watchdog skips a page that takes too long, but it can't stop that page's worker from allocating, so the memory cases end in an allocation-failure abort that takes every open document with it. The negative case leaves a worker spinning on a core until the app exits.

Vendored **hayro** patch (5, 6), marked `PdfCraft patch:` and listed in `vendor/README.md`. `usable_dash_pattern` bounds how many pieces a pattern can cut the path into, in user space where kurbo dashes: (control-polygon length / period + restarts) × entries per period, where restarts are kurbo's own (every `MoveTo` and `ClosePath`). The control polygon is never shorter than the curve.
- Over `MAX_DASHES_PER_STROKE` (250,000) the stroke is drawn **solid**. That is what such a fine pattern looks like anyway, and nothing is dropped.
- A pattern with a negative or non-finite entry, or a period that isn't positive, is drawn solid. ISO 32000-2 §8.4.3.6 requires nonnegative entries.
- A non-finite phase becomes 0.
- Measured in release builds: a 250,000-piece…

title: Export to Word/HTML/RTF: read text and images drawn by form XObjects (fixes #314)
author: SBaksa
body:
Fixes #314.

## What was wrong

`Doc::export_pages` built its paragraphs from `pdfcraft_edit::text_blocks` and its images from `page_images`. Both read only the page's own content streams, because they back Edit text and Edit image, which rewrite those streams. A page drawn through `/Fm1 Do`, which is how many print-to-PDF and document-distribution tools emit pages, therefore exported as an empty document with no error.

## Fix

- **`pdfcraft-edit`:** new read-only `reading_blocks` and `reading_images`.
  - They follow `Do` into form XObjects, including nested ones, and apply each form's `/Matrix`.
  - Each form uses its own `/Resources`, or the caller's when it has none (PDF 1.1 files).
  - Each form starts from the graphics state at its `Do`.
  - Nesting is capped at `MAX_FORM_DEPTH` (12), and a form already being read is skipped, so self-referencing and mutually recursive forms are read once.
- **Shared code:** `interpret` can optionally record the `Do`s it meets. The editing path passes `None`, so its behaviour is unchanged. The line-joining loop of `text_lines` moved unchanged into `add_shown` so both readers share it.
- **`pdfcraft-engine`:** `export_pages` uses the new functions for Word, HTML and RTF. Edit text and Edit image still offer only the page's own content, because text inside a form can't be rewritten in place.

## Tests

- `reading_follows_form_xobjects`: nested forms with their own matrices, fonts and an image. It checks positions, sizes and fonts through every matrix, and that `text_blocks` and `page_images` are unchanged.
- `hostile_form_xobjects_are_read_once`: covers forms that are self-referencing, mutually recursive, missing their resources, carrying a malformed `/Matrix`, or missing entirely.
- `exporting_office_files_reads_form_xobjects`: the PDF from the report, exactly as posted (no xref table, wrong stream lengths). It fails on `main` with an empty export and passes with this change.

title: Never crash: JBIG2 symbol dictionaries can't loop without end
author: jcl-bit
body:
Found by `cargo xtask fuzz` (4 jobs, 300 s, Windows, seeded from the pinned pdf.js corpus). A 1.1 KB page whose JBIG2 image never finished decoding: killed after 120 s at a flat 3 MB. It differs from a valid file by one byte inside a symbol dictionary's arithmetic-coded data. The nightly fuzz job reported a hang from a sibling seed on 2026-10-06 (`Hang from bitmap-symbol-texttopright.pdf`), which may be the same bug; I haven't downloaded that run's findings to compare.

Past the end of its data, the arithmetic decoder keeps returning values. Two loops in `vendor/hayro-jbig2/src/decode/symbol.rs` only move on when those values make progress:

| Loop | No progress when | Found by |
|---|---|---|
| export runs (6.5.10), `export_symbols` | a run of length 0: `index` doesn't advance, and the decoder returned 0 for ever | the fuzz finding |
| height classes (6.5.5), `decode` | a class whose first width is already the end-of-class marker decodes no symbol | a read-only sweep of every loop in the crate. In a synthetic dictionary every class after the first symbol adds 13 to the height, so it only fails when the height overflows `u32`, after 330 million empty classes (about 5 s per image, logged). A delta of 0 never ends. |

The sweep found every other loop in hayro-jbig2 bounded by a symbol, instance or pixel cap, or by the end of the data (the Huffman reader stops there).

- A valid dictionary needs at most one height class per new symbol, and `2 × symbols + 1` export runs. The runs alternate between exported and not, so there is at most one zero-length run before each symbol's.
- Both loops get that budget plus `EXTRA_EMPTY_STEPS` (1024), and past it the dictionary fails as invalid.

title: M3: renders of a dropped render pool stop at the next operator
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

The engine replaces a document's `RenderPool` after every edit, undo or redo, after a layer toggle and after "Hide all comments"; closing the document drops it too. Dropping a pool stopped only its idle workers. A worker in the middle of a page kept interpreting and rasterizing it to the end, then found that nobody could receive the answer and threw it away.

On a heavy page (dense vector drawing, CAD), that is seconds of CPU per worker, spent at exactly the moment the new pool starts re-rendering the same pages. Up to 7 old renders compete with up to 7 new ones, so the page the user just edited takes about twice as long to come back.

## Fix

Two small parts.

**hayro-interpret, vendored patch 17**, marked `PdfCraft patch:`:
- `InterpreterSettings::cancelled: Option<Arc<AtomicBool>>`, defaulting to `None`.
- `interpret` checks it before each content operator and stops when it is set. Nested content (forms, Type 3 glyphs, patterns, annotation appearances) runs through the same loop, and so does text extraction.
- After a `break`, the existing code below the loop restores the graphics-state stack as usual.

**pdfcraft-render:**
- The pool's shared state gets a `dropped` flag, and `impl Drop for RenderPool` sets it.
- Workers build their settings with `cancelled: Some(dropped)` (`worker_settings`).
- `new_inline` assigns the fields it resets one by one instead of using struct-update syntax, which a type with `Drop` doesn't allow. It behaves as before.

**Why nothing visible changes:** the flag is set only when the pool is dropped. By then its result channel is gone, so a cancelled, partly drawn page can never reach the UI; the worker's `send` fails and it exits, as it did before after a full render. A live pool never sets the flag, so its renders are exactly as before. `PageRenderer` (CLI, tests, inline/web pools) never sets `cancelled`.

## Evidence

A local harness (not committed) rendered 7 heavy pages (400,000 filled rectangles each) on 7 workers. It t…

title: Never crash: decompression bombs can't exhaust the renderer's memory
author: jcl-bit
body:
The renderer's parser (vendored **hayro-syntax**) decoded Flate, LZW and RunLength streams with no output limit. title: Never crash: mesh shadings can't exhaust memory or run for minutes
author: jcl-bit
body:
Found by `cargo xtask fuzz` (4 jobs, 600 s, Windows, seeded from the pinned pdf.js corpus), with the fixes from #405, #408 and #411 applied locally. In that run it was the only finding.

**The finding:** a page whose Coons patch shading (type 6) is a 147-byte stream with 1-bit coordinates decoded onto ±40000 took the renderer past 3 GB.
- hayro-interpret samples mesh shadings (types 4–7) pixel by pixel over each triangle's device-space bounding box, into a map with one entry per pixel.
- Only the `u16` cast bounded it: up to 65536 × 65536 entries for one triangle.

Two rounds of review of my earlier versions found more:
- every patch was cut into 722 triangles (about 150 KB) before anything limited them;
- a lattice mesh with `/VerticesPerRow 0` pushed empty rows forever, and one with 4294967295 read the whole stream into one row;
- a mesh painted a thousand times was triangulated a thousand times;

| one Coons patch decoded onto ±40000 | past 6 GB in 6 s, killed | 5 MB, 0.2 s |
| 10,000 triangles each covering half of a 1000 × 1000 page | over 60 s, killed | 55 MB, 0.3 s |
| the two fuzz findings | past 3 GB, killed | 1 MB, 0.2 s |

On the desktop the first is an abort that takes every open document with it. The second is a page the watchdog skips while a worker keeps a core busy.

title: View: keep earlier tiles on screen while a zoom's new tiles render
author: cyfung1031
body:
Follow-up to #363, for the mid-gesture blur reported while pinch-zooming dense pages (#260, page "0.2pt dense grid + 5pt text").

## Problem
When a page is larger than `TILE_THRESHOLD` (4096 device px), it is drawn from 1024 px tiles over a 2048 px whole-page backdrop. Every zoom step dropped **all** tiles of the previous scale before the new ones existed. So during a pinch, each frame fell back to the backdrop, stretched 2–4×, until the new tiles arrived.

## Change (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`)
- **Tile retention.**
  - Tiles are now keyed by `(page, scale tag, x, y)`.
  - Tiles of earlier zooms stay and are drawn stretched under the current ones, farthest scale first and nearest on top.
  - They are kept only while a current tile of their page is still missing: at most 64 of them, nearest scale first, and only for pages within 2 of the current page.
  - Current tiles are still drawn texel-aligned, as in #363.
- **Backdrop.** On entering the tiled range, a whole-page raster that is sharper than the backdrop (rendered just before the page crossed the threshold) is kept, not replaced by the 2048 px backdrop.

Nothing changes once rendering settles: the current tiles cover the page and the older ones are freed.

## Evidence
**Regression test:** `tests/view.rs::zooming_a_tiled_page_shows_its_earlier_tiles_until_new_ones_arrive`.
- It is deterministic: the first frame at a new zoom cannot have its tiles yet, because they are only requested at the end of that frame.
- That frame keeps 90% of the settled detail with this change, against 64% before. The threshold is 70%.

**Headless measurement** (egui_kittest, silent and cross-platform, ppp 2, page 9 of a synthetic test PDF). Each frame of a pinch is compared with an exact render of the same 400×300 device-px window:

| Pinch (30 × 4% steps, 100 → 324%) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| zoom-in: mean abs diff | 9.24 | 5.30 |
| zoom-in: tiled frames (≥ 211%) | ~12 | ~2–4 |

title: Reduce large-PDF memory growth (#307)
author: skylartaylor
body:
Addresses the excessive memory usage reported in #307. Use lazy inspection, shared parser/resource metadata, bounded scan/write caches, visible-page raster budgets, and cached signature discovery while preserving undo state, PDF object semantics, and signature validation.

Measured on the same 9,156-page PDF on Linux, after rebasing onto `a6bc63a`:

| Workload | Before → after peak RSS | Reduction |
|---|---|---:|
| CLI inspection vs original main (`d801407`) | 14.97 GiB before OOM → 497.7 MiB, completed | **96.8%** |
| Full-save workflow | 3.69 → 1.06 GiB | **71.2%** |
| Mixed edit/undo/save/reopen | 4.16 → 1.43 GiB | **65.6%** |
| Desktop navigation/close/reopen | 1,123 → 877 MiB | **21.9%** |

Inspection compares with the original's observed peak before a confirmed kernel OOM at the 15 GiB container limit; its completed peak is unknown. Save rows compare with the earlier opening/navigation optimization; desktop compares with the bounded-writer stage. Full-save values are three-trial medians; other rows are single runs. The current build also includes the intervening upstream changes.

Validation: **1,336 workspace tests and 193 parser tests pass** (6 ignored; 2 missing-fixture parser tests filtered), strict workspace Clippy passes without allowances, and all 30 WASM crate checks pass. All 1,010 navigation frames and 12 workflow artifacts match; eight saved PDFs pass external checks on 100 pages each. Both 1×/2× GUI protocols pass, including upstream render dedup, pixel alignment, signatures, and organizer behavior covered by regression tests.

Tradeoffs: full serialization takes ~43% longer, while the complete full-save workflow takes ~17% less time. Cache budgets are not a global RAM cap. Windows, the reporter's exact PDF, cold-start stalls, and the 1–2 s first-page target remain unverified; the measured desktop open request is ~4.6 s.

title: Print: support Windows printers (fixes #160, fixes #244, fixes #293)
author: AppSunder
body:
## Problem

On Windows the Print dialog only offered \"Save as PDF\". The spooler (\`crates/print/src/spool.rs\`) only knew CUPS (\`lpstat\`/\`lp\`), so \`printers()\` returned an empty list and \`submit()\` reported that printing wasn't available on the platform.

Fixes #160, fixes #244, fixes #293.

## Change

Windows backend in \`spool.rs\`; the CUPS path is unchanged.

- **Printer list:** \`Get-CimInstance Win32_Printer\` through PowerShell, with the default printer flagged.
- **Printing:** the sheets are rasterized with \`pdfcraft-render\` at 200 dpi and streamed over stdin to a PowerShell \`System.Drawing.Printing.PrintDocument\` job. Rasters work with any driver, not only PDF-capable ones.
- **Options:** copies, collation, duplex and grayscale go in as \`PDFCRAFT_*\` environment variables. Paper size is matched to the printer's named sizes when close, else custom; landscape sheets set the landscape flag.
- **Safety:** same stance as #338. No temp files, and no document or printer name is spliced into script text (the script is passed with \`-EncodedCommand\`). Render failures are reported as such rather than as a broken pipe.
- \`pdfcraft-render\` is now a dependency of \`pdfcraft-print\` (no cycle; the engine already depends on both).
- Docs: print README, \`ROADMAP.md\`, and the \`parity/\` note updated.

## Testing

- New unit tests: printer-list parsing, job environment, \`-EncodedCommand\` encoding, and the page stream (3 sheets incl. a landscape page: sizes, BGRA, opaque, drawn).
- \`cargo fmt --check\`, \`cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings\`, \`cargo test -p pdfcraft-print\` and the UI print test pass on Linux. The Windows target also passes clippy (\`x86_64-pc-windows-gnu\`) and builds on a \`windows-latest\` runner.
- The PowerShell job itself was tested by hand on a real Windows PC: printers show up and printing works. It has no automated test, since CI has no printer.

## Known limits

title: Fix: High-precision float mantissa overflow in hayro-syntax, causing warped display of some PDFs  (#199)
author: philkwek
body:
## Summary
Resolves #199 where PDFs with high-precision double-precision float coordinates (e.g. 16+ decimal places output by jsPDF 3.0.3 in `/MediaBox`) rendered severely warped/compressed with large white margins instead of filling the canvas.

## Root Cause
In `vendor/hayro-syntax/src/object/number.rs`, `read_inner` accumulated float mantissa digits into `u64` using `wrapping_mul(10).wrapping_add(...)`. Mantissas exceeding `u64::MAX` (such as 20-digit values) wrapped modulo $2^{64}$, corrupting the mantissa and distorting dimensions (e.g. 3874.96 pt became 185.61 pt).

## Changes
- **`vendor/hayro-syntax/src/object/number.rs`**:
  - Replaced wrapping arithmetic with `checked_mul(10).and_then(|m| m.checked_add(d))`.
  - Discard excess trailing fractional digits beyond `u64` capacity without advancing `decimal_shift`. This preserves full IEEE-754 `f64` precision (53-bit significand) while preventing integer overflow for numbers with arbitrary numbers of decimal places.
  - Saturated integer parsing to `u64::MAX` and fall back to `InternalNumber::Real` for integers exceeding `i64` bounds.
  - Added unit test `high_precision_float_does_not_overflow_mantissa` covering the reported coordinates and an extreme 50-digit fraction.
- **`crates/render/src/inspect.rs`**:
  - Added integration test `jspdf_high_precision_mediabox_does_not_overflow_dimensions` using a synthetic PDF fixture with jsPDF-style high-precision `/MediaBox`.
- **`vendor/README.md`**:
  - Documented patch (6) for `hayro-syntax` and its associated test.
  
  TLDR: Fixed overflow issue by adding logic to drop trailing bits that overflow. Essentially rounds the decimal accuracy down such that it will not overflow.

## Verification
- `cargo fmt --check` passes.
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` passes with 0 warnings.
- `cargo test --offline -p pdfcraft-render` passes (52 tests passed, including `jspdf_high_precision_mediabox_does_not_overflow_dimensions`).

Closes #199

title: Edit text: fast drags on a paragraph's edge no longer get dropped; add a left-edge handle
author: kremit
body:
### Problem

In Edit a PDF ▸ Edit text & images, dragging the rewrap handle on a paragraph's right edge
ignored quick drags. A drag only worked if you pressed, held, then moved slowly.

### Cause

egui reports `drag_started()` only once the pointer has moved past `max_click_dist` (6 points by
default) or the button has been held for `max_click_duration` (0.8 s). `edit_text_ui::page_input` first returned
early unless the pointer was **currently** over a box or the 7x14 px handle, and only then
checked `drag_started()`. On a quick outward flick the pointer had already left the handle by
the frame the drag started, so the one-frame `drag_started` event was lost. Holding first
worked because the long-press threshold fired while the pointer was still on the handle.

`prepare.rs` already does this correctly: it picks the drag target from `press_origin()`.

### Fix

Modify `crates/ui-egui/src/edit_text_ui.rs` to:

- Check `drag_started()` before the hover early-return, and resolve the grabbed box and edge
  from `press_origin()`.
- `Grip { Move, Left, Right }` replaces `resize: bool`. The left edge rewraps too, sending
  `BlockStyle { width, offset: [dx, 0] }`. It uses `user_box` deltas, so it stays correct on
  pages rotated 180°.
- Edge hit zones span the box's full height, +/-6 px around the edge line. Handles are drawn
  on both edges and follow the live edge.

### Tests

New `a_quick_flick_on_either_edge_rewraps_the_paragraph` in `tests/editing.rs`. It presses
on an edge and has the pointer at its destination by the next frame, covering narrowing,
widening outward (the reported bug) and the left edge.

- Without the fix: fails (the outward flick leaves the paragraph wrapped).
- With the fix: passes, along with the existing
  `dragging_a_paragraph_moves_it_and_its_edge_rewraps_it`.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and
  `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui` (41 test binaries, 360 tests) all pass.

title: Fix non-WinAnsi Latin diacritics (ă, ș, ț) in form appearances and support page-level widget annotations

### Summary

This PR resolves two issues related to PDF interactive form fields:
1. **Interactive form fields not detected on certain documents:** Some PDF forms (such as forms created with Adobe PDF Converter SDK or older Acrobat generators) omit the document-level `/AcroForm /Fields` array and define interactive widget annotations directly in `/Page /Annots`. These fields were previously ignored and rendered as flat page content.
2. **Diacritics rendered as `?` when fields are unselected / blurred:** When interactive text fields contained Romanian or Eastern European characters (such as `ă`, `ș`, `ț`, `Ă`, `Ș`, `Ț`), the text displayed properly while focused (inside the editor widget), but rendered as `?` (e.g. `Turnu M?gurele`) when unselected.

   - Standard Type 1 fonts (`/Helvetica`, `/Times-Roman`) in the rasterizer lacked fallback mapping for non-embedded glyphs when `/Differences` were present, defaulting to Foxit's 256-glyph font which lacks extended Latin glyphs.

title: sign: read the .p12 files Windows writes (BER, not DER)
author: feraremag2680
body:
## The bug

Importing a digital ID exported from the Windows certificate store (Protect ▸
digital IDs ▸ "A file" → the `.p12` / `.pfx` Windows writes) fails with:

> PKCS #12: not a PKCS #12 file

The password is never reached — the file is turned away at its **second byte**.

Windows writes PKCS #12 in BER:

* the PFX, its ContentInfo and the `[0]` around the AuthenticatedSafe all use
  the **indefinite length form** (`0x80` … `00 00`, X.690 §8.1.3.6), and
* the AuthenticatedSafe itself is an **OCTET STRING split into segments**
  (constructed, tag `0x24`, §8.21).

`crates/sign/src/der.rs` accepts definite lengths and primitive strings only,
so `0x80` as a length is `"unsupported DER length"` and every one of those
files is rejected. OpenSSL writes definite DER, which is why the fixtures in
`crates/sign/tests/data/` never showed it. On the four Windows-exported files I
had to hand each one starts `30 80`; the two OpenSSL fixtures start `30 82`.

RFC 7292 does not require DER here, so this is a file the reader should take.

This is a **different cause of the same symptom as #159** (the Spanish
government's certificate). #298 fixed that one — whitespace, PEM armour and
base64 around the file — and this fixes the encoding inside it, so the two
compose: `normalize()` still runs first, and what comes out of it is now read
with the BER reader.

## The fix

A `Tlv` now carries the rules it was read with, and its children are read the
same way:

* `Tlv::parse` is the strict DER reader it has always been;
* `Tlv::parse_ber` also takes the indefinite form;
* `Tlv::octets()` returns an OCTET STRING's contents, joining the segments of
  the constructed form, and **borrows** when there is nothing to join, so the
  ordinary path copies nothing.

Both are depth-bounded (48 for BER nesting, 16 for segment nesting) and the
length arithmetic is checked, per the never-panic rules.

Only `pkcs12.rs` reads with the BER reader, and only for the envelope. `x509`
and `cms` keep the strict…

title: Issue #431: reload a document when its file changes on disk
author: pauliusiv123-rgb
body:
Closes #431.

Rebuilding a LaTeX or Typst document now updates the open PDF in place, as SumatraPDF and Okular do. The page, zoom and scroll stay where they were, and nothing flashes. It's on by default, with a switch under **Preferences ▸ Documents and view ▸ Reload documents when their files change on disk** (desktop only; the web build has no files to watch).

**How it stays cheap**
- One worker thread (`pdfcraft-watch`) checks each open file's metadata every 250 ms and doesn't read the file. While no open document has a file, it blocks and never wakes. The UI thread is only woken when there is a new version to show.
- A file's version (`Stamp`) is its length, its modification time, and what the platform adds: Unix device, inode and change time; Windows creation and last-write times. The modification time alone is coarse on FAT and some network drives, and a rebuild can keep the same length.
- A changed file is read only once it has stopped changing (two checks 40 ms apart) and its last KiB contains `%%EOF`. That KiB is read first, so a file pdflatex is still writing costs one small read. The whole file is then read into a buffer of exactly its size, and the stamp is checked again in case a writer replaced the file meanwhile.
- If the file is locked by its writer, missing, or not a whole PDF yet, the open version stays and the watcher keeps looking.
- `Session::reload` runs the full open pipeline on the new bytes and puts the result in the old document's place. Same `DocId`, name and path, and the edit generation moves on, so caches keyed by it refresh.
- `DocView::document_replaced` keeps the reader's place (zoom, layout, rotation, page, scroll, view history, find bar) and the page images on screen until their replacements are drawn. Everything that pointed into the old version starts afresh: selected comment, form focus, text editing, drags, page selection. A shorter new version can't leave a stale index behind.

**Measured** (Windows 11, debug build)
| | |
|--…

**Preferences ▸ Documents and view ▸ Reopen the files that were open when PdfCraft last closed** (desktop, off by default). With it on, PdfCraft remembers the open files when it closes, and at the next start it:
- reopens them in the same order, each at the page it showed, with the same tab in front;
- opens any files named on the command line after them, in front (double-clicking a PDF while PdfCraft is closed);
- skips files that are gone, files about to open from the command line anyway, and documents the Recovery dialog offers after a crash, so nothing opens twice.

**Quitting with unsaved changes:** the save prompt closes each unsaved tab before PdfCraft quits, so the list is taken when the first prompt is answered and dropped if the quit is cancelled. Without that, those files would be missing next time.

**Details**
- New `last_session.rs`. Paths are stored absolute (`std::path::absolute`), so a file opened by a relative path from a terminal is found again from another directory.
- Settings are untrusted: malformed entries are skipped, the list is capped at 64 files, the active tab is matched by path, and `go_to_page` clamps the page.
- Only one password prompt can wait at a time: the first encrypted file asks for its password, and later ones stay closed (they're in Recent).
- While the preference is off, nothing is stored.

The new string is translated in all nine catalogs, with their `ATTRIBUTION.toml` hashes updated. `parity/acrobat-features.toml` has a new entry, `core.reopen-last-session`, whose notes list what's not done yet.

**Tests**

title: Issue #432: global Units preference (mm, cm, in, pt), defaulting to the system region
author: bulgariamitko
body:
Fixes #432.

## Problem

PdfCraft showed lengths in inches with no way to change it. Document Properties (page size), the Print dialog (sheet size) and the Header & Footer margins were hard-wired to inches. The Measure tool fell back to inches on pages without a scale. Set Page Boxes offered millimetres, but always started at inches. People in metric countries, i.e. most of the world (we're a print shop in Bulgaria), had to convert by hand.

## Change

- **Preferences ▸ Documents and view ▸ Units:** mm / cm / in / pt, saved with the other settings (`"units"` in the persisted JSON).
- **Default from the system region on first start** (and for settings saved before this existed), as the issue proposes:

- **Used in:**
  - Document Properties ▸ Advanced ▸ Page size (`210.0 × 297.0 mm`).
  - The Print dialog sheet size.
  - Header & Footer margins (label, values, drag speed and decimals).
  - Set Page Boxes: starts in the preference, can still be changed per dialog; Centimetres added.
  - Measure tool: a page without a viewport scale now measures true size in the preferred unit. `measure::scale_at_or` / `Document::measurement_scale_or`; `scale_at` and `measurement_scale` are unchanged (inches), so automation and existing callers behave as before.
- New `ui-egui/src/units.rs` (`Unit`, shared with pageboxes, which used to define its own).
- Translations: "Margins (in)" became "Margins" plus the unit; the new hint "For page sizes and margins." is added to es, fr, ja, ru, te, zh-hans and zh-hant, and `ATTRIBUTION.toml` hashes are updated.

title: M4: zoom the Organize page grid
author: samehelhawary
body:
## What

The Organize page grid drew every page in a fixed 190 × 250 pt cell, so text on the pages could not be read and there was no way to see more pages at once. The grid now zooms from 50% to 300% (parity entry `organize.thumbnail-size`).

title: M2: handle Unicode dates and preserve inspection fallback pages
author: Streetblock
body:
An annotation `/M` string such as `D:12345678901éX` could panic when date formatting sliced through a UTF-8 character. Auxiliary inspection had already swapped renderer pages into temporary metadata; unwinding dropped those pages and opening then reported that the document had no pages.

Check the date prefix safely and preserve non-date strings. Stage auxiliary metadata using cloned renderer geometry and commit it only on success, retaining the original pages and reporting a warning on failure.

Three synthetic regressions cover UTF-8 boundaries, opening a generated PDF with a UTF-16BE annotation date, and preserving geometry while discarding partial metadata after a panic or error. They reproduce the old failures before the fix.

Validation on Linux x86_64 in Docker with Rust 1.95 and the project's pinned craft-fonts build input:

- `cargo xtask ci`: all eight gates passed (fmt, strict workspace Clippy, workspace tests, layering, WASM, assets, dependency audit and parity).
- `cargo check -p pdfcraft-cli --no-default-features`: passed.
- CLI `doc_open`, `doc_info`, `comment_list` and `page_render` under `--root`: the generated Unicode-date PDF opens, preserves the annotation text and renders at 100×150 pixels without inspection warnings.

title: M2: bound lopdf predictor scratch to available samples
author: Streetblock
body:
Empty PNG predictor frames still reserved row buffers from the declared width. For 1/2/4-bit TIFF Predictor 2, a 64-byte decoded stream could overflow row-size arithmetic or panic while allocating an accumulator from a huge `/Colors` value.

Return empty PNG data before reserving buffers, reject overflowing TIFF row sizes, and size component scratch to samples actually present. Valid packed rows retain component wrapping, independent rows and padding bits. The TIFF changes align with the existing upstream [lopdf#589](https://github.com/J-F-Liu/lopdf/pull/589); the vendored patch and its tests are recorded in `vendor/README.md`.

Four synthetic regressions cover empty frames, overflowing dimensions, excessive colors, and valid 1/2/4-bit rows. The malformed cases reproduce the old failures before the fix. This bounds predictor scratch relative to available input; it does not introduce a global memory limit.

Validation on Linux x86_64 in Docker with Rust 1.95 and the project's pinned craft-fonts build input:

- `cargo xtask ci`: all eight gates passed (fmt, strict workspace Clippy, workspace tests, layering, WASM, assets, dependency audit and parity).
- `cargo check -p pdfcraft-cli --no-default-features`: passed.
- All 55 render-crate tests passed, including the four added regressions.

title: M7: pick a Japanese fallback face that has every glyph of the edited text (#384)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #384.

**What the user saw.** Replacing text in a serif line (Times New Roman, for example) with Russian or other Cyrillic text failed with "Edit text failed: Japanese fallback font has no glyph for U+0444" (or U+0420, and so on).

**Cause.** If the original font cannot show the new characters, the editor draws them with a Type 3 font built from a craft-fonts Japanese face. `type3_font` took only the style's first face. For serif text that is Shippori Mincho, which has no Cyrillic. BIZ UDMincho and BIZ UDPGothic ship alongside it and both have Cyrillic. I checked the `cmap` tables of the craft-fonts files: Shippori Mincho lacks П р и в е т ф, and the two BIZ UD faces have all of them.

**What changed.**
- `pdfcraft_fonts::document_japanese_fonts_for_style` lists every Japanese face in the existing order of preference. `document_japanese_font_for_style` still returns the first one, so its callers are unaffected.
- `type3_font` uses the first face that has a glyph for every character of the replacement. Text that the preferred face can show keeps that face, so Japanese text is unchanged. If no face has all the characters, the preferred face still names the missing character, as before.
- No fonts or assets are added.

**Tests.**
- `cyrillic_in_a_serif_line_falls_back_to_a_face_that_has_it` (needs craft-fonts, which the Linux CI job has): replaces a Times-Roman line and paragraph with "Привет, world", then checks the text after save and reopen. Without the fix it fails with the error from the issue.
- `fallback_face_moves_on_when_the_best_face_lacks_a_character`: uses synthetic faces to test the choice of face.
- `document_faces_match_style_without_inventing_missing_weights`: now also checks the full candidate order, with no face listed twice.

I could not build this locally because I have no Rust toolchain here. CI will run fmt, clippy and the tests.

title: M1: enforce decoded limits on unfiltered COS streams
author: Streetblock
body:
`Stream::decoded_within(2)` returned all three bytes of an unfiltered `abc` stream despite its documented output limit. The same bypass affected empty `/Filter` arrays and streams whose `/Crypt` filter had already been applied. Xref parsing relies on this API's tighter structural bound.

Check the raw output length against `min(max, MAX_DECODED)` before copying. Strict decoding shares the raw guard for its existing per-stream limit. Public signatures and filtered decoding behavior remain unchanged. This protects the returned copy; it is not a document-wide memory budget.

Five tiny synthetic tests cover the raw variants, exact and zero-byte boundaries, and the existing Flate limit. Three regressions fail on the original product code and pass with the guard.

Related: [#162](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/162) proposes `decoded_strict_within(max)` but retains the same raw-copy bypass; that new branch should also use this guard when integrated.

Validation on Linux x86_64 in Docker with Rust 1.95 and the project's pinned craft-fonts build input:

- `cargo xtask ci`: all eight gates passed (fmt, strict workspace Clippy, workspace tests, layering, WASM, assets, dependency audit and parity).
- `cargo check -p pdfcraft-cli --no-default-features`: passed.
- Headless CLI `doc_open`, `doc_info` and `page_render`: a generated one-page PDF opens without inspection warnings and renders at 100×150 pixels.

title: i18n: let the layers below hand their sentences over, so they can be translated
author: feraremag2680
body:
## What this is

The interface is translated into ten languages, but a good part of what a person actually reads in the Accessibility panel, the PDF/A list, the signature details, the print dialog and the edit history was still English in every one of them. Those sentences are worded by the layers below the UI, and `notify_error` says why they were left alone:

> Engine and OS messages are not translated: matching their English wording would break silently whenever it changes.

That is exactly right, so this doesn't try to match the wording from the outside. It has each layer hand its own wording over, apart from the document's own words, and lets the UI look it up.

## The arrangement

Each layer that words sentences gains three things, in its own vocabulary:

- `pub const WORDINGS: &[&str]` — every sentence it can say, written once, with holes in it (`{n}`, `{p}`, `{}`).
- `said(&self, words: Words) -> String` — says one of them: look the wording up through the closure, then fill the holes with the document's values in a single pass, so a file name containing `{n}` goes in as written.
- `pub fn in_english(wording: &str) -> String` — the closure that changes nothing, for the CLI, the automation layer and the tests.

The UI passes `&crate::i18n::words`, which is a catalog lookup. A wording with no catalog entry comes back as it stands — which is the English — so a catalog that is missing one shows an English sentence rather than a gap, and the nine catalogs this PR doesn't touch keep reading exactly as they do today.

Because the sentence is now data the layer publishes rather than a literal duplicated in the UI, it cannot drift: change the wording and the catalog entry stops matching, which is what the tests check.

## What changed

**Engine side.** `a11y::Finding`, `preflight::Issue`, `sign::pdf::Detail` and `print::PrintError` carried pre-formatted English `String`s; they now carry the document's values and name their wording. `Edit::label()` likewise returns a `…

title: M2: bound page-label traversal and output
author: Streetblock
body:
PDF page labels could expand large `/St` values into very long Roman or repeated-letter strings. A depth cap also left the inspector exposed to repeated and wide number trees. In the editor, Roman formatting was unbounded and alphabetical formatting silently truncated long labels.

Use shared bounded PDF numeral formatters and validate label processing before applying its results:

- At most 10,000 combined tree-work entries and a depth of 32; check children and number-pair counts before staging them and detect repeated nodes or cycles.
- Check raw prefixes before decoding (2,050 bytes), complete UTF-8 labels (1,024 bytes) and aggregate custom-label output (4 MiB).
- Preserve ordinary Roman and PDF repeated-letter numbering, Unicode prefixes and prefix-only ranges. Check numbering arithmetic where a number is used.
- Stage inspector labels and retain physical page numbers with one warning on failure. Checked editor reads and setters return an actionable error before changing the number tree; the existing String-returning preview formatter documents its decimal fallback.

Small synthetic regressions reproduce the old failures without excessive allocations. Additional cases cover exact boundaries, hostile numbers, wide trees, aggregate output, references and refused edits retaining the original tree. The shared helpers are pure COS code; rendering adds only an existing workspace dependency.

Validation on Linux/x86_64 in a resource-limited Docker container, using the pinned craft-fonts checkout:

title: Comments: a new highlight opens its note for typing (#475)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #475.

**What the user saw:** after highlighting text, the highlight appeared in the Comments panel without a text field for the note. The field only showed up after double-clicking the card. Acrobat opens the note for typing as soon as the highlight is made.

**Cause:** `apply_edit` selected and revealed every new comment, but only a double-click or the card's Edit menu set `comments.editing`, the panel's inline editor.

**What changed:** for a new highlight, `apply_edit` (`crates/ui-egui/src/editing.rs`) also opens that editor. Every highlight path goes through it: dragging over text, picking the tool with text already selected, and area highlights. If a note typed into another card is still unsaved, the editor stays there and the new highlight is only selected, so the typed text is not thrown away. Other comment types are not changed. The `comment.highlight` parity entry now mentions this and cites the test.

**Tests:** `a_new_highlight_opens_its_note_for_typing` (`crates/ui-egui/tests/comments.rs`) checks that the editor opens for a text highlight and for an area highlight, and that an unsaved typed note is kept when another highlight is made. Without the fix, `editing` stays `None` and the test fails.

title: M10: Print ▸ Properties… opens the printer driver's own settings
author: bulgariamitko
body:
## Print ▸ Properties… (the printer driver's own settings)

The Print dialog had no way to reach the printer driver's settings (Acrobat's **Properties** button): paper tray, paper type, output tray, stapling, Fiery queue actions and so on. Print shops need these every day. This adds a **Properties…** button next to the printer list; it is disabled for Save as PDF.

### CUPS (macOS, Linux): per job, inside the dialog
- `spool::printer_options(printer)` reads the queue's PPD (`/etc/cups/ppd/<queue>.ppd`, capped at 16 MB, UTF-8 or Latin-1). It overlays the queue's current defaults from `lpoptions -p <queue> -l`, so the user's `~/.cups/lpoptions` counts too.
- `parse_ppd` keeps each `OpenUI` option with its label, group and choice labels. It skips:
  - the `InstallableOptions` group (hardware setup, not job settings);
  - options the dialog already sets (`PageSize`, `PageRegion`, `Duplex`, `Collate` …);
  - multi-line PostScript inside choices, and translation lines (`*fr.InputSlot`).
  It is lenient and bounded (keywords validated, at most 400 options and 400 choices).
- The dialog shows them grouped as the driver groups them. Only choices changed from the printer's defaults are kept, and they go to `lp` as `-o key=value` for **this job only**. "Reset to printer defaults" clears them. Options read for one printer are never sent to another.

### Windows: the driver's Printing Preferences window
Opening a driver's per-job settings (`DocumentProperties`) needs `unsafe` FFI, which the workspace forbids. So on Windows the button runs `rundll32 printui.dll,PrintUIEntry /e /n "<printer>"`: an absolute path, the name quoted, no shell. That is the same window as Settings ▸ Printers ▸ Printing preferences. What is set there becomes that printer's per-user default, which every job starts from; the dialog's copies, two-sided, grayscale and paper still apply on top. The tooltip says so. On `main` Windows lists no printers yet, so the button only becomes useful together with #421.

title: Export to Word: detect tables of at most 63 columns, Word's limit (#479)
author: Erige005
body:
Fixes #479.

Word opens tables with at most 63 columns, but table detection accepted up to 64 (`ncols <= MAX_COLS` with `MAX_COLS = 64`). A page detected as exactly 64 columns produced a `.docx` that Word refused to open. `MAX_COLS` is now 63, so such a grid stays paragraphs like wider ones already do. The constant also caps HTML and RTF tables, which lose one column of headroom. The staircase bound it was added for still holds.

### Test

`word_opens_tables_up_to_its_column_limit` exports regular grids of short numbers: 63 columns still becomes a 63-column table, and 64 columns now produces no table. Its 64-column assertion fails on `main`.

### Checked

- `grid64.pdf` from #479 exported with `pdfcraft-cli`: on `main` the `.docx` has a 64-column table and Word (Microsoft 365, Windows) fails to open it. With this change it has no table and opens.

title: M2.6: non-embedded Mincho fonts draw half-width katakana
author: chent11
body:
## What the user sees

Text in a non-embedded Japanese Mincho font (HeiseiMin-W3, MS-Mincho, …) draws kanji and full-width kana correctly since #368, but **half-width katakana (U+FF61–U+FF9F) come out as unrelated glyphs**: Latin letters and ligatures such as ﬁ and ﬂ. Half-width katakana are common in Japanese documents, for example for name readings on forms.

![Before and after: half-width katakana in a non-embedded HeiseiMin-W3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chent11/pdfcraft/pr-evidence/before-after.png)

Synthetic test file: [halfwidth-katakana.pdf](https://github.com/chent11/pdfcraft/raw/pr-evidence/halfwidth-katakana.pdf) (HeiseiMin-W3, not embedded, `UniJIS-UCS2-H`). Rendered with `pdfcraft-cli run` + `page_render`, built with craft-fonts.

## Cause

For a Mincho name, `japanese_fallback` returns `document_japanese_font()`, i.e. Shippori Mincho. Shippori Mincho has none of the 63 half-width katakana. hayro maps the CID through Adobe-Japan1-UCS2 to Unicode, finds no glyph in the face's `cmap`, and falls back to drawing the CID as a glyph index, which lands on unrelated glyphs.

## Change

- The Mincho substitute in the renderer is now **BIZ UDMincho Regular**, which covers all half-width katakana (and was designed as a metric-compatible replacement for MS Mincho). It falls back to `document_japanese_font()` when BIZ UDMincho isn't built in.
- The face used for Japanese text *written into* PDFs is unchanged. Builds without craft-fonts are unchanged.
- No fonts or assets are added.

**Visible side effect:** all text in a non-embedded Mincho font now draws in BIZ UDMincho rather than Shippori Mincho, so glyph shapes change slightly. For example, the "CID CJK font sample" line on page 2 of #260's `pdf_engine_test.pdf` is still correct, but its Latin letters are narrower. If you'd rather keep Shippori Mincho's look, an alternative is to keep Shippori Mincho and fall back per glyph. I went with the smaller change, but I'm happy to rework it.

title: Phone photos follow EXIF orientation; image signatures stay upright on rotated pages (#434)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Part of #434. Complements #473 (image stamps on rotated pages): this PR covers JPEG EXIF orientation and image signatures on rotated pages.

#473 leaves these two out: image-file orientation metadata and image signatures. This PR does not touch custom stamp placement, and it does not change any of the lines #473 changes. The two commits can be reviewed on their own.

## 1. JPEG EXIF orientation (first commit)

**What the user saw:** a portrait photo from a phone, used as a custom stamp or added as an image, showed up on the page turned 90 degrees, although it looked upright in every image viewer.

**Cause:** phones store a portrait photo as landscape pixels plus an EXIF Orientation tag. `pdfcraft_create::image_xobject` embeds a JPEG as it is (DCTDecode), and a PDF image XObject has no orientation, so the tag was lost. Fill & Sign image signatures already applied the tag (`signature_image.rs`). The other paths did not: custom stamps, Add Image, Replace Image, updating an added image, watermark and background images, and button images (`SetFieldImage`).

**Change:** those call sites in `crates/engine/src/lib.rs` now go through `embed_image`, which passes the bytes through the new `upright_image::upright` first. A JPEG whose Orientation is not 1 is decoded, turned with `DynamicImage::apply_orientation` and re-encoded at quality 92. Its JFIF resolution is kept, swapped for quarter turns, so the natural size on the page stays right. Grayscale stays grayscale. Everything else is embedded unchanged, as before: PNGs and other formats, JPEGs without the tag, JPEGs that fail to decode, and photos over 64 megapixels. Create PDF from images is not changed here.

## 2. Image signatures on rotated pages (second commit)

**What the user saw:** on a page with `/Rotate` 90, 180 or 270, a Fill & Sign image signature (the GUI, or `fill_sign_add` with `path`) turned with the page instead of reading upright. It was also anchored at the wrong point: at displayed `[60, 100]` on a 90 degre…

title: CI: serialise fill_sign pixel renders (Windows ARM64 WARP access violation)
author: AutoHenry
body:
## Problem
The `test (native ARM64)` job in the **Windows ARM64** workflow intermittently fails on main: the `fill_sign` test binary dies with `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` (0xc0000005) while every test inside it is passing.

```
error: test failed, to rerun pass `-p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test fill_sign`
process didn't exit successfully: `...\fill_sign-7b0782d2983718f0.exe` (exit code: 0xc0000005, STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION)
```

Seen in runs 37876160101 and 37867887465 (main) and 37861778584 (PR).

## Cause
The image-signature tests added in #335 / #355 call `h.render()` from parallel tests. The ARM64 runner has no GPU, so wgpu falls back to WARP, whose ARM64 pixel-shader JIT crashes when two devices compile shaders at once. `tests/view.rs` documents this and serialises its renders with a `GPU` mutex, as does `tests/document_links.rs`; `fill_sign.rs` never took it.

## Fix
Add the same `GPU` mutex to `crates/ui-egui/tests/fill_sign.rs` and take it first in the six tests that render pixels (declared before the harness, so it's released after the wgpu device is dropped). kittest creates the device lazily on the first `render()`, so tests that don't render are unaffected and still run in parallel. Test-only change, no product code touched.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test fill_sign`: 14 passed (macOS)
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --tests -- -D warnings`: clean
- The Windows ARM64 workflow's path filter means it won't run on this PR. Since the crash is intermittent, the real confirmation is consecutive green ARM64 runs on main after merge, or a manual `workflow_dispatch` of "Windows ARM64" on this branch if a maintainer wants to check before merging.

A possible fix, for a separate PR, is to have the integration tests pin the language explicitly, for example by setting it to English in the shared test-harness setup, rather than relying on `cfg!(test)`.

title: Never crash: CMap parsing can't panic, overflow or run away; tokens need no spaces
author: AutoHenry
body:
## What was wrong
`crates/fonts/src/pdf.rs` parses ToUnicode and embedded CID CMaps by splitting the stream on whitespace and slicing hex tokens as UTF-8 text. All four of these reproduce on main (a6bc63a):

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `<0é0>` in a `bfchar` | **panic**: `end byte index 2 is not a char boundary` (`hex_bytes`) | token ignored |
| `bfrange <FFFFFFFE> <FFFFFFFF> [<0041> <0042> <0043>]` | **panic**: `attempt to add with overflow` | maps the 2 codes in range |
| `/Differences [9223372036854775807 /A /B]`, `cidrange ... 4294967295` | unchecked `as u32` / `+= 1` / `c + (code - lo)` | saturating |
| 200 `bfrange`s of 65 536 codes (4 KB) | 13 M map entries | capped at 1 Mi entries |
| `beginbfchar<0001><0070>…endbfchar` (legal, no spaces) | maps nothing | maps |

The last row is user-visible. A synthetic Type0 PDF whose ToUnicode is written without spaces gives, through `pdfcraft-cli run` → `text_paragraphs`:
- main: `"paragraphs": []`: no text is found, so nothing can be edited
- this PR: `"text": "present"`

This *may* be what's behind #347 (the edit box shows `)&*+*$`), but that issue has no attached file, so I can't confirm it.

## Change
- A small byte-level lexer for CMap syntax: `<…>` hex strings (whitespace inside allowed, odd/invalid → ignored as before), `[`/`]`, names, `(…)` literal strings with nesting/escapes, `<<`/`>>`, `%` comments.
- `parse_to_unicode` and `parse_cmap` read entries from it. Entries end at their `end…` operator even when a section is short.
- Checked or saturating arithmetic on every code counter. Array-form `bfrange` stops at `hi`, and a malformed array entry still uses up its code, as before.
- Limits: at most `MAX_CMAP_ENTRIES` (1 Mi) ToUnicode insertions and `MAX_CMAP_RANGES` (64 Ki) codespace/CID ranges, since every glyph searches these linearly. Real CMaps are far below both.

Only this file changes. None of the open PRs that touch it (#447, #357, #252) change the parser.

title: Issue #225: a closed Comments panel stays closed when picking comment tools
author: AutoHenry
body:
Fixes #225.

## Problem
Picking any comment tool opens the Comments panel whenever no right panel is open (`commands.rs:188`). Once you close it, the next switch to a comment tool opens it again. Two users report this, on macOS and on Linux/Xfce.

## Change
- New `PdfCraftApp::choose_right_panel(Option<RightPanel>)` for opens and closes the user makes:
  - Closing Comments, from its close button or the rail icon, sets `comments_panel_closed`.
  - Opening Comments again clears it: the rail, the View menu, `comment.list`, or a Reply / "open Comments" action on the canvas.
  - Switching to another panel, or closing one, doesn't count as closing Comments.
- Comment tools only open the panel when `!comments_panel_closed`, so Acrobat's default (tools open Comments) is unchanged until the user closes it.
- The flag is saved in settings (`comments_panel_closed`), so the choice survives a restart.
- `set_option("panel", …)` (control channel and CLI) still sets the panel directly and doesn't record a choice.

**Left as is, open to a different call:** opening a document that has comments still shows the Comments panel (`lib.rs:793`), as Acrobat does. If you'd rather a closed panel also stay closed there, it's a one-line follow-up.

This doesn't conflict with #481 (a new highlight opens its note), which changes `editing.rs`.

## Tests
`tests/comments.rs::a_closed_comments_panel_stays_closed_when_picking_comment_tools` covers this sequence:
1. Picking a tool opens Comments.
2. Clicking **Close** closes it.
3. Highlight, Underline, Note and Select (in turn) leave it closed.
4. The flag survives `persist()` → `restore()`.
5. Clicking the rail's **Comments** button reopens it and clears the flag.
6. Switching to Bookmarks and closing that panel leaves the flag clear.
7. Strikeout opens Comments again.

Without the fix, the test fails with "comment.underline reopened the closed Comments panel".

**Preferences ▸ Date format** sets the text that Fill & Sign ▸ Date stamps:

author: vuski
body:
Korean file names in the tab strip and Korean bookmark titles render as replacement boxes (#407). No embedded face has Hangul (the release-pinned craft-fonts input has only Japanese faces, and craft-fonts `main` has no `Kore`/`Hang` face either), so Hangul falls through to the installed fallback. That fallback is chosen by probing for Arabic alef, which picks Segoe UI on Windows, and Segoe UI has no Hangul.

This adds a second installed UI fallback for Hangul, chosen by probing for U+AC00 가:

| Platform | Candidates, best first |
|---|---|
| Windows | `malgun.ttf` (Malgun Gothic), `gulim.ttc` |
| macOS | `AppleSDGothicNeo.ttc`, `Supplemental/AppleGothic.ttf` |
| Linux / FreeBSD | Nanum Gothic (Debian, Fedora, Arch paths), UnDotum, Baekmuk Dotum |

Noto Sans CJK is deliberately not a candidate, since §1.1 names it as Source Han rebranded.

`installed_font_definitions` adds the Hangul face to every family after every embedded face. The existing broad-coverage fallback stays last. Hangul doesn't overlap the scripts of the embedded faces, so the order doesn't change how other text is drawn. The same `MAX_BYTES`/`MAX_FACES` bounds and the `PDFCRAFT_SYSTEM_FONTS=0` opt-out apply to both faces. The face is read at runtime only and is never embedded, copied, shipped or used in a PDF.

`system_fonts.rs` keeps `fallback()` and gains `hangul_fallback()`, with `load(paths, probe)` shared. That is the same shape #426 uses for its Chinese face, so the two PRs should combine with a small merge.

**Maintainer decision requested:** `AGENTS.md` §1.4 currently allows one installed font. This PR proposes wording that allows one Hangul face plus the existing broad-coverage face. #426 asks for the same kind of change for a Chinese face. PhotoCraft already does this for its UI: storytold/photocraft#185 (for storytold/photocraft#149) reads installed CJK faces, Malgun Gothic and Gulim among them, as interface fallbacks. title: Two pages at a time: a page display that turns spreads instead of scrolling
author: vuski
body:
Two-page view scrolls its spreads continuously. There is no way to read a document a spread at a time, the way Single page shows a page at a time. This adds a fourth page display for that, **Two pages at a time** (`view.layout.two_page`, `two-page` in settings and view options, Lucide `book-open`).

Behaviour, matching Single page:
- One wheel notch or trackpad swipe, Page Down / Page Up and → / ← move one spread. Zoomed in far enough to pan, the wheel pans instead.
- Fit page fits the spread on screen.
- The cover page setting applies: [1], [2, 3], [4, 5], …
- On the last spread, Next stays put instead of stepping to its second page.

PDFs whose `/PageLayout` is `/TwoPageLeft` or `/TwoPageRight` ("display the pages two at a time", the catalog's `PageLayout` entry, ISO 32000-2 §7.7.2) now open in it. `/TwoColumnLeft` and `/TwoColumnRight` still open in Two-page view.

The code reuses what is there: the spread stepping from #77, the wheel pager that Single page uses, and the Two-page view row layout. `PageLayout` gains `paged()` (Single page, Two pages at a time) and `two_pages()` (Two-page view, Two pages at a time), and the places that tested for `Single` or `TwoUp` use them.

**Design suggestion:** to keep the change small, this adds a new menu entry. I think a cleaner model would be to make Continuous scrolling an option that combines with the others: without it, one page or two pages always turn a page (or spread) at a time; with it, they scroll. That is also how `/PageLayout` is structured (`SinglePage` / `OneColumn`, `TwoPageLeft` / `TwoColumnLeft`). It would change the existing menus and settings, so I'd rather hear what you think before doing it.

Translations: the new label "Two pages at a time" needs an entry in every catalog whose coverage test checks all registered commands, so I added one to cs, es, fr, ja, ru, te, zh-hans and zh-hant, and updated their `ATTRIBUTION.toml` hashes. title: Issue #125: page text the standard fonts can't draw is refused, not written as ?
author: AutoHenry
body:
Fixes #125. See also #194 and #222 (the added-text part).

## Problem
`page_add_text`, `doc_header_footer` and `doc_watermark` (and the matching UI) write every character outside WinAnsiEncoding as `?`, then report success. On #327 you said refusing is right for these page-content tools ("there the `?` *is* the page content"), but not for form fields or text-box comments. This PR does the page-content part only.

## Change
- **fonts:** `win_ansi_encodable(c)` and `first_non_win_ansi(s)`. Both are defined through `win_ansi` itself, so when #447 fills in the missing WinAnsi characters (Œ, Š, ƒ…) these widen with it. The edited-text Type 3 decision (`edit/src/text.rs`, `is_win_ansi_char`) now uses the same check; the character set is identical to the old hand list.
- **edit:** one `drawable(lines)` check that runs before anything is changed. It is called from:
  - `added.rs::validate`, which covers both adding and updating
  - `add_header_footer`, on the templates (tokens only add ASCII; Bates prefixes and suffixes are part of the template)
  - `add_watermark`, for text watermarks only

  Each caller passes its text split the way it draws it: `split('\n')` for added text, `.lines()` for headers and watermarks. So a CR that would be drawn as `?` is refused, but CRLF in a header isn't.

  Error: `the standard fonts can't draw "中" (U+4E2D); only Western European characters can be added as text for now`
- **UI (Add text):** the editor shows the warning, translated, under the text box while it contains such a character. It doesn't commit or lose the text:
  - Done, a click elsewhere, or a double-click on another item leave the draft as it is
  - the draft counts as unsaved work, so closing prompts
  - Save stops, scrolls to the draft and shows the warning
  - "Don't save" still closes
  - deleting the draft's page drops the draft with it, so nothing is left blocking Save out of sight

title: Issues #444, #186: a mouse wheel scroll speed preference, faster by default on Windows and Linux
author: AutoHenry
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This changes the default for every Windows and Linux user, and it hasn't been tried there by a person yet.** At the default (Normal) setting, one wheel notch moves 100 pt instead of 40, everywhere: documents, side panels, dialogs and menus. On macOS and the web the default doesn't change, so my Mac testing never showed the faster speed. The automated tests run on all platforms, but nobody has *felt* 100 pt with a real Windows or Linux mouse. I've asked the reporters of #444 and #186 to try this branch. Please wait for at least one of them, or someone on the team, before merging.

Fixes #444. Fixes #186.

## Problem
egui scrolls `line_scroll_speed` = 40 points per wheel line on the desktop. winit reports a Windows wheel notch as 1.0 line (`WM_MOUSEWHEEL` / 120) and an X11 button click as 1.0 line, so a notch moves 40 pt. Browsers move about 100 px per notch on Windows, so both reports say the wheel is too slow and ask for a setting.

## Change
- **Preference:** Preferences ▸ Documents and view ▸ **Mouse wheel scroll speed**: Slow / Normal / Fast.
  - These are 0.5×, 1× and 2× of the platform's normal speed.
  - Normal is **100 pt per line on Windows and Linux**, **40 on macOS** and **8 on the web**. macOS and the web keep egui's defaults: macOS already accelerates line deltas, and the web's line deltas are scaled differently. So nothing changes on macOS or the web unless the user picks Slow or Fast.
  - New module `crates/ui-egui/src/scroll_speed.rs`.
- **When it applies:** in `raw_input_hook`, before egui's `begin_pass` reads the options, so a change takes effect from the next input. It is also set in `logic`, for hosts that don't call the hook (kittest, for one).
- **⌘/Ctrl-wheel zoom keeps egui's rate.** egui multiplies line deltas by `line_scroll_speed` before turning them into zoom. Without compensation, one zoom notch would have gone from 1.22× to 1.65× (2.72× at Fast), so those events are scaled back in the hook. Plain wheel events and point…

title: M7: Hebrew in Edit text (reading order, writing order, Hebrew glyphs)
author: tzagim
body:
## Problem
On Windows, a Hebrew PDF displayed correctly, but Edit text broke it in two ways:
1. **Reversed text:** "בדיוק" appeared letter-reversed. Content streams draw right-to-left lines in visual order, and `text_lines` concatenated glyphs in that order.
2. **Replacement boxes:** when the page's (subset) font lacked a letter, Edit text fell back to Helvetica/WinAnsi or the Japanese Type 3 face. Neither has Hebrew.

## Changes
- **`pdfcraft-edit::bidi` (new):**
  - `to_logical` turns a line read from a content stream into typing order. `to_visual` turns typed text into drawing order, using UAX #9 through `unicode-bidi`, which was already in `Cargo.lock`.
  - Handles numbers, Latin inside Hebrew, mirrored brackets, and combining marks kept on their letter.
  - Visual order can have more than one logical reading. Readings are checked by round trip: only one that draws back exactly as the page did is accepted, and one with paired brackets is preferred.
  - Also handles producers (LibreOffice) whose ToUnicode maps a bracket drawn in an RTL run to its logical character.
- **`text_lines` / `text_blocks`** now return typing order. This also fixes the text the automation tools (`text_lines`, `text_paragraphs`) and Compare see.
- **`replace_line` / `rewrite_block`:**
  - Both encode each line in drawing order.
  - Right-to-left paragraphs are right-aligned unless an alignment is chosen. A single RTL line keeps its right edge and grows to the left.
  - A justified RTL paragraph ends its last line at the right edge.

title: M3: the watchdog stops the render it gives up on
author: cyfung1031
body:
Follow-up to #409.

## Problem

When a render runs longer than `stuck_after` (20 s), the watchdog does three things: it answers with an error, starts a replacement worker, and drops the late result. The abandoned worker, though, kept rendering the page to the end. #409's stop flag belonged to the whole pool and was set only when the pool was dropped.

On a document with several very heavy pages (dense vector or CAD drawings), up to `threads` abandoned renders keep CPU cores busy beside their replacements. They are working on answers that will be thrown away.

## Fix

`crates/render/src/raster.rs` only. No API change and no new patch to the vendored interpreter: it uses #409's `InterpreterSettings::cancelled`.

- Each worker gets its own stop flag (`Shared::stop`, indexed by worker id like `busy`), created in `spawn_worker` and passed to the worker.
- `Drop for RenderPool` sets every worker's flag, which is #409's behaviour unchanged.
- `watchdog()` sets the flag of the worker whose slot it clears, under the same `busy` lock, so that render stops at its next content operator.

**Why nothing visible changes:** the watchdog has already answered for that request with an error, and the worker drops its late result (`abandoned`), as before. Only the wasted work stops. Live workers' flags are never set.

`vendor/README.md` (patch 17) now mentions the watchdog and the new test.

## Evidence

A local harness (not committed) used 4 workers and 4 heavy pages. Each page shows a form 40,000 times, and the form is 2,000 operators that draw nothing. `stuck_after` was 300 ms. After all 4 "took longer" errors arrived, it measured the process's CPU time over the next 3 s, when there was nothing left to do. Apple M1 Pro, two runs each:

| | CPU used in the 3 s after the watchdog gave up |
|---|---|
| `main` | 11.6 s, 11.2 s (about 4 cores still busy) |
| this branch | 0.0 s, 0.0 s |

## Tests

- **New: `raster::tests::the_watchdog_stops_the_render_it_gives_up_on`.** One worker, a page…

title: M1: full saves are allocated at their exact size
author: cyfung1031
body:
Follow-up to #402, which made incremental saves exact-size.

## Problem

`write_full` can't know the output size in advance. Its buffer starts empty and grows by doubling, so the result kept up to as much again as unused capacity.

That result is often kept for as long as a document is open:

- **Working bytes after a full rewrite.** `write_incremental` falls back to `write_full` for repaired files, security changes and redaction (`crates/cos/src/writer.rs:179`). The engine then keeps the result as the document's working bytes, shared with the render pool, after every such edit.
- **Save As ▸ optimized:** `save_full_bytes` (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs:2498`), then `mark_saved`.
- **Every new document** from Create, Combine, Extract and Split goes through `write_new` (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs:2792`).

## Fix

```rust
out.shrink_to_fit();
Ok(out)
```

This is placed at the end of `write_full` in `crates/cos/src/writer.rs`.

- It changes only capacity, never contents, so the output bytes are identical.
- On macOS the shrink happens in place: 2 µs for a 100 MB buffer, and the buffer doesn't move. Allocators that can't shrink in place copy the buffer once, which is small next to serializing the document.

## Evidence

A local harness (not committed) ran `write_full` on generated documents of 200 pages. Release build, Apple M1 Pro, best of 3:

| Size, object streams | Unused capacity before | After | Time before → after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 MB, on | 1.4 MB (27.9 %) | 0 | 1 → 1 ms |
| 5 MB, off | 5.0 MB (99.2 %) | 0 | 1 → 1 ms |
| 40 MB, on | 11.2 MB (28.0 %) | 0 | 6 → 5 ms |
| 40 MB, off | 14.8 MB (36.9 %) | 0 | 5 → 5 ms |
| 100 MB, on | 28.0 MB (28.0 %) | 0 | 14 → 15 ms |
| 100 MB, off | 31.6 MB (31.6 %) | 0 | 11 → 13 ms |

## Test

`cos/tests/writer.rs::full_saves_are_allocated_at_their_exact_size`: the fixture plus a 100 KB stream is saved in full, with and without object streams. For each, it checks:

- `capacity == len`;
- the result reopens with an empty repair lo…

title: M7: edit text: Cyrillic/Greek replacement text no longer fails in serif lines, and is spaced proportionally
author: bulgariamitko
body:
## What was wrong
Edit text sends replacement text to the Type 3 fallback when the line's own font can't show it (subset fonts carry only the glyphs already used) and WinAnsi Helvetica can't either. For serif lines that fallback was always **Shippori Mincho**, which has no Cyrillic or Greek. So retyping a word in a Bulgarian (or Russian, Ukrainian, Greek) document failed on the first new letter:

```
text_edit: Japanese fallback font has no glyph for U+0421
```

The other bundled faces have these letters. Coverage of the Bulgarian alphabet (А–Я, а–я, ѝ), checked with fontTools:

| Face | Missing |
|---|---|
| Shippori Mincho Regular | all 61 letters |
| BIZ UDMincho Regular | ѝ only |
| BIZ UDPGothic Regular / Bold | ѝ only |

Found on a real Bulgarian book PDF (Ghostscript, Garamond-Bold subset): with #495 applied the lines become editable, but changing "Плевен" to "София" still failed.

## Change
- `pdfcraft_fonts::document_font_for_text(serif, bold, text)`: returns the style's face (`document_japanese_font_for_style`, unchanged) when it has a glyph for every character. Otherwise it returns the closest other `Jpan` face that does, Mincho first for serif text and then the requested weight. It returns `None` when no face can show the text.
- `type3_font` uses it and falls back to the style's face as before, so a character that no face has still gets a clear error naming it. That message now reads "no fallback font has a glyph for U+…" instead of "Japanese fallback font…".
- **Spacing.** These faces draw Cyrillic and Greek full-width (1 em per letter, as in JIS X 0208), and none of them has `palt` metrics for those letters. A replaced word therefore came out letter-spaced ("С о ф и я"). Fallback glyphs in the Greek and Cyrillic blocks are now advanced by their ink width plus a 0.05 em side bearing on each side. Every other character keeps the face's own advance.
- Japanese text is unaffected: Shippori Mincho has every Japanese character it had before, so it is still …
