title: fix(sign): refuse to sign a field whose /V is not a signature (#1328)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Follow-up to #1374, as suggested there (issue #1328).

After #1374, a signature field whose `/V` is null (direct or indirect) is unsigned and can be signed. A `/V` that is neither null nor a signature dictionary, though (an empty string, a number, a name, an array…), was also treated as unsigned and silently overwritten on signing. Now that case is refused with "the value of the field … is not a signature", and nothing is written. Missing or null `/V` still signs, and a real signature is still "already signed".

`list_cached` still lists such fields as unsigned, since they hold no signature. So the UI still offers "Sign this field…", and the attempt now fails with a message that says why. Marking them as invalid in the list would need a new wording and its translations; happy to do that separately if you'd like it.

Validation:
- `a_field_whose_value_is_not_a_signature_is_refused_by_name` covers an empty string, a number, a name and an array, each direct and indirect. On main it signs (`Ok(…)`).
- Dropping the null exception fails `a_field_with_a_null_value_is_unsigned_and_can_be_signed`, so both sides are pinned.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(forms): keep a whitespace-only value in a text field without a format (#1323)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1323.

`keystroke` treated any whitespace-only input as "clear the field", whatever the field's format. In a plain text field (no number/date/… format) a value of a single space or tab was therefore emptied. Whitespace-only input now clears the field only when a format applies. An empty string still clears any field.

Validation:
- `tests::whitespace_only_text_is_kept_in_a_field_without_a_format` covers a space, a tab and an NBSP, with an empty-string control.
- Two new asserts in `af::tests::numbers_format_like_acrobat` check that formatted fields still clear.
- On main the first gets `[]` instead of `[" "]`.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-forms -p pdfcraft-xfdf` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(content): skip an inline image with an unreadable key to its EI (#1318)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1318.

When an inline image's dictionary had a key or value the parser couldn't read, `inline_image` gave up and returned `data.len()`. Everything after the `BI` was dropped (the issue's `q BI … EI Q BT … Tj ET` parsed as `[q, BI]`), and none of it was counted as skipped. Now the parser looks for the matching `EI`, counts `BI`…`EI` as skipped bytes and carries on after it. The damaged image is dropped rather than kept as a half-read `BI` that would re-serialise as a different image. Without an `EI` the behaviour is unchanged. The `EI` search moved into a small `end_of_image` helper as-is.

Validation:
- `tests::an_unreadable_inline_image_is_skipped_to_its_end` gets `[q, BI]` on main and `[q, Q, BT, Tj, ET]` here.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-content -p pdfcraft-edit` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(automation): doc_save reports a required full rewrite as not incremental (#1329)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1329.

`doc_save` reported `"incremental": !full`. But `write_incremental` falls back to a full rewrite when it has to (protection, Remove Hidden Information, rebuilt files), and the flag still said `true`. It now reports `!full && bytes.starts_with(saved_bytes)`: a save is incremental only when the output really extends the bytes it was opened from. That needs a read-only `Document::saved_bytes()` accessor in the engine. The cos writer is unchanged; the cost is one prefix comparison.

Validation:
- `an_in_place_save_reports_a_required_rewrite_as_not_incremental`: a rotate stays `true`, while `doc_protect` and `doc_remove_hidden` must report `false`. On main `doc_protect` reports `true`.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation -p pdfcraft-engine` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: feat(preflight): verify image resolution and bleed without rewriting the file
author: Baltsar
body:
Follows the review on #1230. This is verification only. Nothing in the file is rewritten.

`print_readiness` is a read-only headless tool. It reports:

- Effective resolution where each image is drawn, from the placement matrix. A 100 px image drawn across 144 pt is 50 ppi, not "100 px on the page". Images that only appear inside a form XObject use the existing optimizer measurement (the smallest use). Below 150 ppi is a failure. Below 300 ppi is a warning.
- The page boxes that are actually in the file (media, crop, trim, bleed). Bleed is a warning when the tightest side past the trim is under 2 mm. A missing TrimBox or BleedBox is not invented.
- Output intents. A screen profile (sRGB, Adobe RGB, display) is a warning when no press profile is declared. No ICC profile is generated, and no Adobe profile name is used.
- Fonts that are not embedded. They are reported, not embedded.
- The existing PDF/A-2b structural result. This does not claim PDF/A-1b, PDF/A-4, or PDF/X.

Out of scope, on purpose: content-stream rewriting, hairline or action fixups, stripping encryption, a press-profile conversion, a dialog, and any parity row marked shipped.

Test: `ocr::printcheck::tests::a_drawn_image_is_measured_where_it_is_placed` (50 ppi fails on the drawn size, 600 ppi does not, bleed is warned only where the boxes say so).

The branch history is noisy. The diff against main is the change, so a squash merge is the right landing.

Credit as @Baltsar is enough. I have not added a `people.toml` entry.

title: fix(render): draw Turkish Ğ İ Ş ğ ş in non-embedded fonts
author: TheLastRoadRunner
body:
## Problem

Turkish letters Ğ, İ, Ş, ğ and ş render as blanks in PDFs whose fonts aren't embedded, while ı, ç, ö and ü in the same text render fine. A real case is a letter produced by iText 2.1.7: its fonts are Times New Roman (`TimesNewRomanPSMT`, `-BoldMT`, `-ItalicMT`), not embedded, and they use `/Differences` with `/Gbreve /Idotaccent /Scedilla /gbreve /scedilla /dotlessi` over the WinAnsi codes for Ð Ý Þ ð þ ý.

## Cause

Non-embedded fonts are drawn with the standard-14 stand-ins in `vendor/hayro-interpret/assets` (PDFium's Foxit fonts, CFF). Each carries about 230 glyphs, only those of the Standard, WinAnsi and Mac Roman encodings. `dotlessi` is in StandardEncoding, so ı draws. `Gbreve`, `gbreve`, `Idotaccent`, `Scedilla` and `scedilla` aren't in the stand-ins, so `StandardKind::map_code` falls back to `.notdef` and nothing is drawn. The same happens to most Latin Extended-A letters: Polish ą ę ł ń ś ź ż, Czech č ě ň ř, Romanian ă, and so on.

## Fix (vendored hayro-interpret patch 26)

When the stand-in lacks such a letter, `StandardKind` builds it from the base letter and accent the stand-in does have, the way Type 1 `seac` composites and the standard-14 AFM composites are built:

- The accent is centred on the letter. Over capitals and letters with ascenders it is raised by the difference between the letter's top and the top of `x`. In italic stand-ins it is also moved along the slant.
- Cedillas hang below the letter, and ogoneks from its right edge.
- A composite gets a glyph id above any font's glyph count, one per character code (`COMPOSITE_GLYPH_BASE + code`). `outline_glyph` builds the outline from that code. The width comes from the standard metrics of the glyph's name, as for other stand-in glyphs.
- The table, `ACCENTED_LETTERS`, holds the Latin Extended-A letters made of one plain accent. ď ľ ť and the comma-accented letters are left out.

It adds no assets and no dependencies. Text extraction is unchanged; it already mapped these names to Unic…

title: fix(audit): an identity cm between re and fill no longer hides a cover (#1333)
author: umesh429
body:
Fixes #1333.

The faux-redaction audit missed a black cover when an identity matrix sat between the rectangle and its fill (`100 688 220 32 re 1 0 0 1 0 0 cm f`). `crates/audit/src/cover.rs` cleared the pending `re` rectangle on every `cm`, so the fill had nothing to record.

Now `cm` clears the pending rectangle only when it actually changes the CTM. A matrix that does change the CTM still clears it, as before, so behaviour for real transforms mid-path is unchanged.

Test (`crates/audit/src/tests.rs`): `identity_matrix_between_rectangle_and_fill_still_covers_text` checks both the identity-after and identity-before streams from the issue. Each must give one `CoveredText` finding with rect `[100, 688, 320, 720]` and text `SECRET DATA 123`. The identity-after case fails without the fix (0 findings). The existing controls (text-only, background before text, translucent and light covers) still give no findings.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` all pass.

title: fix(ui): Current page prints the viewed page, not a page labelled with its number (#1308)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1308.

Print › Current page passed the page as the range token `"N"`, and ranges read page labels first. So in a document whose labels don't match positions (e.g. i, ii, 1, 2…), Current page could print a different page that happened to be labelled with that number. Current page now goes through `print::select_listed(count, &[current_page], …)`, the same path Selected pages uses. A typed range still reads labels as before.

title: M14: Hebrew interface language and a right-to-left interface
author: 613avi
body:
Adds Hebrew (עברית, `he`) as an interface language. Arabic and Hebrew now get a real right-to-left interface: bidirectional text layout and a mirrored layout. Before this, labels were only reordered when the catalog loaded.

## Hebrew catalog
- 2,192 entries, covering every command, All tools entry and `tl!` literal. Gender-neutral modern Hebrew, translated clean-room from the meaning of the English labels.
- `he`, every `he-*` locale and the legacy `iw` code select it. Counts use one/other plural forms. Dates use Hebrew month and weekday names.
- Fonts: a craft-fonts `Hebr` face is used if one exists, and the web build keeps it. craft-fonts has no Hebrew face yet, so on desktop a second installed fallback face covers Hebrew.

## Right-to-left interface
- **`vendor/epaint`: bidi text layout (UAX #9).**
  - Each paragraph reads in the direction of its first strong character.
  - Runs are shaped in their own direction but stored in logical order, so line breaking is unchanged, and each row is reordered for display.
  - The caret lands on the correct side of right-to-left letters, and direction marks are invisible.
  - Text with no right-to-left characters skips all of this.
- **`vendor/egui`: `Style::mirror_layout`.** It mirrors rows, columns, grids and text fields. In a mirrored layout, scroll areas anchor and scroll from the right.
- **PdfCraft:**
  - Catalogs stay in logical order, and file names start with an LRM so `.pdf` stays at the end.
  - The docked Tools and Inspector panels and the rail swap sides. The saved layout is unchanged.
  - Hand-painted rows measure from the start edge (`crate::mirror`).

title: Fix Lab Bradford adaptation to use LMS white-point ratios
author: FredApps
body:
Follow-up to #1237; related to #1203. The earlier merged work fixed the reported Lab conversion and Indexed scaling, but follow-up review found that non-D65 white points still acquire a tint because Bradford LMS values are scaled using XYZ white-point ratios.

For example, D50 Lab (50, 0, 0) renders as RGB (126, 117, 118) instead of neutral (119, 119, 119).

Give Lab its own Bradford adaptation using both white points transformed to LMS. Preserve CalRGB's existing flat-white/black-point pipeline and the merged Lab Indexed/Range scaling. Zero or non-finite source cone responses fall back to unadapted XYZ.

Six render regressions cover independent D50/equal-energy neutral and chromatic oracles, D65 identity, direct/Indexed consistency, an asymmetric chromatic Range, and zero/overflowing-cone fallback. The original four regressions produce three failures on base while D65 passes; all six pass with this change. A separate f64 implementation supplies frozen expectations, and external Poppler agrees with all 16 ordinary/asymmetric reference patches. Independent read-only review found no blocking issues.

Validation after a normal merge of upstream 87b448b (commit 1c8b2b0), exact tree 0375169cbc6ebd6aee36b8dc238026b8f0d2f768:
- All 262 render tests pass; workspace: 2,852 passed, 13 ignored, no failures.
- Formatting, strict workspace/all-target Clippy, layers, Wasm (31 crates), assets, and parity pass. The local cargo-deny gate skips because cargo-deny is not installed; no dependencies change.
- Workspace tests use `cargo test --workspace -- --test-threads=1` with `RUST_TEST_THREADS=2`, keeping parent suites serial while a CUPS child stand-in retains its normal output format. Standard runner attempts exposed an unrelated forms timing failure and that child-harness formatting issue; isolated forms and the complete final workspace run pass.
- Rebuilt CLI `doc_open`/`page_render` matches all six ordinary, asymmetric, and fallback pixel controls.

title: fix(content): count an unreadable inline image with no EI as skipped (#1318)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Follow-up to #1404, as suggested there (issue #1318).

When an inline image's parameters can't be read and there is no `EI` after them, `inline_image` still returned the image as a `BI` op with whatever parameters it had read and no data, running to the end of the stream, so those bytes were dropped without being counted. It now returns `Err(data.len())`, so `parse` skips the image and counts `BI` to the end of the stream in `skipped`, the same as #1404 does when an `EI` is found. A stream that ends inside the parameters (`BI /W 1`) has nothing unreadable in it and still gives a `BI` op, and a readable image whose data is cut short keeps its data, as before.

Validation:
- New test `an_unreadable_inline_image_without_ei_is_counted`: fails on main (a `BI` op, `skipped` 0), passes with the fix
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-content --lib`, plus the inline-image tests in `pdfcraft-redact` and the content tests in `pdfcraft-edit`
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-content --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean

title: M4: Fix Combine duplicate warnings and cache their computation
author: LabDennis
body:
Combine files used to warn that different PDFs had been added twice whenever their names and byte lengths matched. Both Grid and List now require matching bytes as well. Actual duplicate additions still warn, and split parts of a single source remain exempt.

Both views use one duplicate check, cached against the existing list revision. Candidate grouping by name and length avoids reading unrelated file contents; exact byte-slice keys distinguish candidates without relying on hash uniqueness. Adding, removing, rearranging, undoing and redoing list entries invalidate the result through the existing revision mechanism. Closing the tab clears it.

This also removes List view's all-pairs scan on every redraw. An isolated optimized microbenchmark with 1,000 differently named files measured approximately 2.27 ms per call for the previous scan, 0.17 ms to rebuild the new result, and 0.01 microseconds to reuse it on an unchanged frame. These are helper timings, not whole-application frame-time measurements; reading same-name/same-size candidates on a changed list still costs time proportional to their contents.

Two UI regressions failed before the fix and now check distinct contents, genuine duplicates, undo and redo in both views. A unit test checks cache reuse, source parts, removal, undo and closing the tab. The existing page-splitting tests remain in place. Headless screenshots were inspected with system fonts disabled.

title: M8: Bound and reuse repeated redaction overlays
author: LabDennis
body:
Applying a redaction with repeated overlay text allocated one owned string per row and then the entire drawing stream from the annotation's declared geometry. Oversized marks could therefore demand unbounded allocations, including outside the page.

Prepare appearances before changing the document, with an 8 MiB budget shared by all selected pages. Checked repeat counts and lengths bound the working row before allocation; every emitted PDF byte counts toward the output budget. Excessive or invalid appearances return an actionable `OverlayLimit` error. A small private overlay module builds, measures and encodes each repeated row once and reuses it. The budget limits generated appearance content, not input PDF size or whole-process memory.

Regression coverage checks rejection before mutation, a shared budget across pages, selected-page application, extreme geometry, escaped WinAnsi text, exact ordinary output, and engine document/undo preservation. The bounded rejection test failed before the fix; it generated about 11 MiB rather than attempting an OOM. A repeat-disabled control still applies successfully.

Performance probe (Windows, `low-disk` profile, mean of 20 helper calls): the 8000 × 800-point repeated-X case produces the same 2,841,859 bytes in 1.56 ms versus 14.39 ms before (~9.2× faster). Output lengths and hashes match across all four measured sizes. This is an appearance-generation microbenchmark; application latency and process peak memory were not measured. The ignored timing probe is included for reproduction.

Validation (Windows, locked dependencies, low-disk profile):
- Formatting, strict Clippy for the changed crates, and all 31 WASM crate checks pass.
- Full workspace at upstream 4a44eea: 2,821 passed, 4 known pre-existing failures, 15 ignored. title: fix(print): custom pages-per-sheet counts no longer overfill sheets (#1336)
author: MrPranklin
body:
Fixes #1336.

`Layout::multiple(n)` turns a count without a fixed grid into a near-square grid (3 → 2 × 2, 5 → 3 × 2), but `Layout::Multiple` kept only `cols` and `rows`, so `layout` filled every cell. Asking for three per sheet put four pages on a sheet, and five put six.

`Layout::Multiple` now carries `per_sheet`, set by `Layout::multiple`. `layout` places at most that many pages on each sheet; it reduces a count larger than the grid to the grid size, and it refuses 0. The spare cells stay blank, and cut-stack piles use the same count. The automation `doc_print` tool and the print dialog now pass the count through instead of dropping it. The dialog only offers 2/4/6/9/16, whose grids already matched, so in practice this changes the CLI/MCP and library results, not what the GUI does.

This adds a field to a public enum variant. Every place in the workspace that builds `Layout::Multiple` is updated. Code outside the workspace that builds it by hand would need to add the field.

Validation:
- `custom_pages_per_sheet_never_overfill_the_grid` covers 7 pages at 3, 5, 7, 4 and 2 per sheet, cut-stack order with 3 per sheet, a count larger than the grid, a count of 0, and the page count of the imposed PDF. Its first assertion fails on main (`[[0, 1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]]`) and passes here.
- Manually, `pdfcraft-cli run` with `doc_print` on a synthetic 7-page PDF reports 3 sheets at 3 per sheet (groups of 3, 3 and 1) and 2 at 5 per sheet; 4 and 2 per sheet are unchanged.
- `cargo test --workspace` passes, and `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: Perf: defer marker and link index scans until first use
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Review direction

Review the lazy-index lifecycle and its consumers for correctness: zero marker/link scans on ordinary open, one shared marker/added-content scan on first request, one link scan on first request, and precise invalidation after relevant edits, comments, undo and redo. These mechanism tests and unchanged ordering/index semantics are the acceptance evidence. Time and memory below are separate sanity observations on the three named PDFs; they do not establish correctness. Hosted CI is not used as evidence, and no hosted result is claimed.

## Summary

- `Session::open` initializes the marker/added-content and editable-link indexes lazily.
- Marker and added-content accessors share one `OnceLock`; repeated access reuses the scan result.
- Link edits refresh the document view while preserving marker state. Comment changes invalidate links because `LinkItem.index` is a position in `/Annots`.
- UI and automation consumers use the accessors. Canvas reads added content only in content-edit mode and links only for link tools.
- A focused counter test covers zero scans on open, cached first use, edit scopes, annotation-index shifts, and undo/redo.

## Problem and root cause

Opening a document eagerly enumerated edit markers, added content and editable links even when a caller only needed ordinary document information. Those scans scaled with annotations and marked content and repeated work for callers that never requested those indexes.

## Target and invariants

Keep `Session::open` free of marker and editable-link enumeration. Materialize each index on first use, share the marker/added-content scan, and invalidate only state whose source data changed. Preserve link ordering, annotation indices, marker semantics, and undo/redo behavior.

## Fix

The document stores lazy marker and link indexes. Content edits invalidate the marker index when their scope changes markers or added content; link edits refresh document state without discarding marker data; comme…

- After a save, File > Revert restores that saved version even if a later edit was undone. It no longer falls back to the file as first opened (#1310).

- [ ] Save a page deletion and a rotation, undo the rotation, set the title, and save. The file should still begin with the rotated revision, and the title should be a newer revision with the rotation undone.

author: marcoarnulfo
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1306.

`ui.move` checks that its coordinates are still finite once narrowed to `f32`, but `ui.click {x, y}` and `ui.drag` did not, so a finite JSON number such as `1e39` became an infinite pointer position and was queued as input. title: MCP: confine file access with --automation-read-root and --automation-write-root
author: isaac-levine
body:
`pdfcraft-cli mcp` gives the agent on the other end the same file access as the user running it. `--root` already confines a session to one folder for reads and writes. VectorCraft has two flags that split the two kinds of access, and its docs say the other Craft apps take the same ones so one client config works across the suite. This adds them here with the same names and behaviour:

    pdfcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root /work/project --automation-write-root /work/project/out

This is the same change as storytold/gridcraft#480 and storytold/wordcraft#798, so the three can be reviewed together.

Every file a tool reads has to be inside the read root and every file it writes inside the write root. A root left out grants none of its access, so the read root alone makes the server read-only. Paths are made absolute, symlinks followed (for a file that doesn't exist yet, the nearest existing folder is resolved and the rest must be plain names), then compared with the root by whole path components, so `/work2` is not inside `/work`. On Windows case is ignored and device names like `CON` and `NUL` are refused. Refusals come back as normal tool errors with VectorCraft's wording, for example `automation path rejected: outside the read root /work/project: /etc/passwd`.

**Where the checks live**

Every path a tool reads or writes already went through `Automation::resolve`, which `--root` uses. That function now also checks the path against the automation roots, so there is no new set of call sites. Two places needed more than that. `doc_save` without a `path` saves in place, to wherever the file was opened from, so it is checked against the write root too. And `text_font_files` without `directories` used to list the installed fonts, which are outside any root, so with roots it searches the read root instead (and is refused if there is no read root). The OCR pre-check of its input paths is now a read check rather than a write check.

The path logic is in `crates/automat…

title: Windows: open a path a launcher passed unquoted and split at its spaces (closes #1455)
author: magdale76
body:
Closes #1455.

Programs that build the reader's command line themselves sometimes leave the path unquoted (`pdfcraft.exe P:\Archive\00042A26 Contract.PDF`). Windows splits it at the spaces, and PdfCraft tried to open each piece ("Couldn't read 00042A26: os error 2"). Acrobat accepts this, so switching such a program's setting from Acrobat to PdfCraft broke opening.

**Change** (`apps/pdfcraft/src/main.rs`): `rejoin_split_paths` runs on the file arguments before the single-instance hand-off. When an argument names no file but it and the following ones, joined with one space, name an existing file, they're rejoined (longest run first, at most 32 pieces). Arguments that exist on their own, or that no run turns into a file, are kept as given, so a genuinely missing file is still reported by its own name. Options (`--…`) aren't affected.

**Limit:** runs of several spaces can't be recovered, since the split has already lost them.

**Tests**
- `unquoted_paths_with_spaces_are_rejoined`: the reported case, the longest run winning, existing files left alone, nothing to join, empty input.
- By hand on Windows 11: launched the built `pdfcraft.exe` with an unquoted path containing a space, as the office program does. The file opened in a tab (checked through `--control` inspect and screenshot); before the change it showed the error. Also confirmed on the reporter's office PC with the program's "open all PDFs" button, via the batch-file workaround, which passes the same joined path.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p pdfcraft --bins`.

title: fix(text): keep doubled narrow letters in condensed text
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1467.

The fake-bold dedupe in `arrange()` treated a glyph as a redraw when the same character sat less than a fifth of its height away. A narrow letter in condensed text is narrower than that (Helvetica `l` at 80 Tz is 0.18 em), so the second `l` of "Alle" was dropped and a word gap inferred in its place. A real redraw also overlaps most of its own width, so the horizontal tolerance is now capped at half the glyph's width; a neighbouring letter starts a full advance away and can't match. Zero-width glyphs (combining marks) keep the old height-based test, since half of nothing would never match an exact redraw of a mark.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed

title: M7: keep line breaks when editing a multi-line paragraph (#1443)
author: rp6186030
body:
Fixes [storytold/pdfcraft#1443](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/1443)

Problem
Adding a word to the end of a multi-line paragraph either merged all its lines into one or reflowed lines that hadn't changed. The report has no sample file. Two independent causes produce this symptom, and both are fixed here.

1. Subset fonts that leave default-width glyphs out of /W (Chrome, Skia)
A composite subset font may omit from /W every glyph whose width equals /DW (ISO 32000-2 §9.7.4.3). Metrics::has_glyph treated a CID missing from /W in a subset as a missing glyph. As a result:

encode failed for any word containing such a letter (s, y, k in Liberation Sans), so source_width dropped those words when measuring;
each run's width calibration (rect width / nominal width) became inflated, up to its 2.0 clamp, so unchanged rows measured wider than the paragraph and rewrapped;
newly typed letters fell back to Helvetica.
Reproduced with a Chromium print-to-PDF page: before the fix, every row of the paragraph rewrapped on a one-word edit.

2. Text drawn rotated on the page
Line joining (text_lines, add_shown) and row/block grouping (group_layout) compared baselines and gaps in raw user space. For text drawn a quarter turn round (0 1 -1 0 … cm, common on landscape pages), every line of the paragraph has the same user-space y. So all lines joined into one TextLine, the editor opened with one row, and the rewrite drew one line. The styled region rewrite also lays rows out along the page's x axis, which is wrong for rotated text.

Fix
fonts: a composite subset font that declares an explicit /DW counts a CID absent from /W as present. This check only runs for codes the font's ToUnicode already maps, so letters the subset never kept are still rejected. Fonts without an explicit /DW behave as before.
edit, geometry: TextLine::frame_origin / frame_rect and a Pen helper express positions along and across each text's own baseline. For upright text these are exactly the old user-spa…

title: M13: Bound automation text caching and preserve partial search results
author: LabDennis
body:
Searching a large document previously retained every extracted page's glyphs and geometry for the document's lifetime. A single page extraction failure also aborted `text_find`, discarding useful matches from readable pages. This bounds retained text data and returns explicit partial search results.

Fixes #1483.

- A dedicated LRU cache shares a 64 MiB estimated text-allocation budget and a 4,096-page bookkeeping limit across all open documents. Accounting includes vector and glyph-string capacities. Oversized pages bypass retention, evicted pages remain re-extractable, revisions invalidate old entries on the next text request, and closing a document clears its entries.
- Cache entries weakly identify the PDF revision, so they cannot keep an obsolete PDF byte buffer alive. Extraction passes the renderer's `Arc<PageText>` through instead of deep-copying all glyphs. Entirely cached requests no longer construct an unnecessary extraction renderer.
- Cache population preserves a separate result for each page. `text_find` keeps readable matches, continues after failed pages and reports bounded, machine-readable warnings. Text extraction, comment placement and redaction retain strict failure semantics.
- Search order, match rectangles and `next` continuation arguments are preserved. `complete` is false for either failures or additional matches; `next` is present only for the latter. Clients should follow `next` when present and inspect warnings separately. The tool description and automation README document the additive warning fields and their limits.

Regression coverage uses generated PDFs and deterministic extraction-failure injection: a 200-page scan across two documents, LRU recency, capacity accounting, oversized/empty pages, re-extraction, revision changes, close, successful pages surrounding errors, capped continuations, missing worker results and bounded Unicode warning messages. The unchanged upstream cache was also exercised with a synthetic probe: it retained…

title: Desktop: prepare large PDFs off the UI thread
author: cyfung1031

title: M2: keep byte boundaries in packed TIFF-predictor rows
author: MMexicann
body:
Packed RGB images with TIFF horizontal differencing can lose every row after the first when a row ends partway through a byte. A valid two-row image renders red then black; Poppler renders red then green.

The shared LZW/Flate TIFF-predictor decoder calls `BitWriter::split_off` while the writer is still partway through the last byte. Align the writer at each row boundary so the next row cannot overwrite the row just returned. This applies to the shared predictor path without changing PNG predictors. Document the vendored patch and update the M2 roadmap notes without changing estimates.

title: M4: preserve shared Type 3 glyph resources during extraction
author: MMexicann
body:
Extracting a page can delete an image used inside a Type 3 glyph when the font's resources share an XObject dictionary or resource owner with the page. The saved PDF remains syntactically valid, but a visible glyph disappears: a synthetic baseline drops from 3,562 to 961 dark pixels and Poppler reports `XObject ImB unknown`.

The XObject pruner reads page/form content, but does not interpret Type 3 glyph programs. Its existing safeguard covers only fonts that inherit the page resources. Protect the resource-owner graph reachable from explicit or inherited Type 3 resources, including nested forms, patterns and soft masks. The walk is iterative, never decodes stream data, tracks references and has a 10,000-item budget including direct children. If the budget is exhausted, leave pruning alone. Memoize explicit resources of shared indirect fonts so large repeated-font documents still prune unrelated page images. Discover glyph resources even when page/form content cannot be decoded.

Validation:

- Save/reopen regressions cover shared XObject dictionaries, shared owners with inline XObjects, nested forms, cycles, unreadable page/form streams, a 20,000-child budget fallback, and 4,000 pages sharing one font. A separate-resource control verifies ordinary unused-image pruning still works.

title: COS: index cross-reference entries on demand
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary

- Retain valid classic xref tables as subsection ranges and decode an individual table entry only when requested.
- Retain xref-stream decoded bytes with `/W` and `/Index` metadata, then resolve entries on demand. This avoids per-object `BTreeMap` node expansion; Flate xref streams still require bounded full-stream decompression.
- Resolve revisions newest-first, preserve hybrid stream precedence and free-entry behavior, and keep explicit sorted object-number iteration. Oversized or unsupported layouts use the existing materialized compatibility path; compact retention is bounded to 2,000,000 rows and 64 MiB of decoded xref bytes.

title: fix(ui): dragged added text follows the pointer before release
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1488.

Added text is part of the page raster, and during a move `content_ui` only redrew the selection box, so the text stayed where it was until the edit landed on release. Still the case on main. title: Add a Nix flake (NixOS, GNOME and Hyprland)
author: untypequicode
body:
## What

Adds `flake.nix` and `nix/package.nix` so that `nix build`, `nix run` and an overlay give a source-built pdfcraft and pdfcraft-cli on NixOS, modelled on the existing LightCraft flake.

- `Cargo.lock` drives the dependencies (git sources through `cargoLock.allowBuiltinFetchGit`), so there is no `vendorHash` to maintain. The version comes from `[workspace.package]`.
- Installs the desktop file, hicolor icons, MIME types and AppStream metadata from `packaging/linux/`, validated at build time (`desktop-file-validate`, `appstreamcli`).
- Wayland and X11: the binaries are wrapped so the libraries winit/wgpu/rfd `dlopen` are found on NixOS — `libwayland-client`, `libxkbcommon` (incl. x11), the X11 libs, the Vulkan loader, `libEGL` and `libdbus` (xdg-desktop-portal file chooser). It runs natively on Wayland under GNOME and Hyprland, with X11/XWayland as fallback. Hyprland needs a portal backend for the file dialogs (`xdg.portal.extraPortals = [ pkgs.xdg-desktop-portal-gtk ]`); this is noted in `nix/package.nix`.
- The fonts from `storytold/craft-fonts`, where the app embeds them, are a pinned non-flake input at the revision the release workflow uses.
- Also: `overlays.default`, `apps.default`, a dev shell, `nix fmt` and a formatting check.
- `rustc` from nixpkgs is linked to an older LLVM than the one this Rust release targets, which breaks `rten-gemm`'s AVX512-VNNI kernels (`intrinsic signature mismatch for llvm.x86.avx512.vpdpbusd`). The flake therefore builds with the official toolchain from `oxalica/rust-overlay` (bundled LLVM, like CI).
- `doCheck` is off: the suite needs corpora and a GPU the sandbox cannot provide (`cargo xtask ci` stays the gate); it can be turned on with `overrideAttrs`.

No Rust, packaging or CI file is touched.

## Testing

`nix build .#pdfcraft` builds both binaries and passes the desktop-file and AppStream validation, on NixOS.

title: fix(organize): normalize rotations before adding so large quarter turns cannot overflow
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
`rotate_pages` added the page's current `/Rotate` to the requested angle before reducing it mod 360. A valid but huge multiple of 90, such as 9223372036854775800, overflows when added to a page rotated by 90: debug builds panic at `crates/organize/src/lib.rs:165` with "attempt to add with overflow", and release builds wrap and write `/Rotate 74`. A file is enough to trigger it: an out-of-range `/Rotate` in the PDF reads as `i64::MAX`, so an ordinary 90 degree rotation of that page overflows too.

The fix reduces both the current rotation and the requested angle mod 360 before adding them, so the sum stays below 720 and the result is unchanged for every rotation that did not overflow.

The first commit adds my contributor display name to `contributors/people.toml`.

## How it was tested

- New regression test `rotate_handles_large_quarter_turns` covers positive and negative angles near the i64 limits and a non-zero remainder, with both page-local and inherited `/Rotate`.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-organize rotate_handles_large_quarter_turns`: fails on unchanged main with "attempt to add with overflow"; passes with the fix.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-organize`: 102 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps passed.

title: Allow mouse-wheel scrolling during text selection
author: FredApps
body:
Fixes #721.

## What and why
egui's ScrollArea ignores mouse-wheel scrolling while a widget owns a drag. PDFCraft's text-selection drag therefore blocked the mouse wheel even though precision touchpad scrolling already had a separate path.

Allow the existing processed Line/Page wheel delta through while the primary text-selection drag owns the canvas. Keep the existing focus, modal, viewport and gesture-ownership guards. Precision touchpad input retains its separate path, including suppression of its eased tail.

This addresses wheel scrolling during the current page's text selection. Edge autoscroll, cross-page selection and the separate sticky-Ctrl zoom report are outside this change.

title: Issue #1396: remove an imported digital ID
author: Ridzzz0Alam
body:
Closes #1396

## In short

Once you imported a certificate (a digital ID) to sign PDFs PdfCraft kept it in the list **forever**. There was no button or menu to remove it. This PR adds a **Remove** button to the **Sign with a Digital ID** dialog.

## Why does it happens

The digital IDs you add whether you import a `.p12`/`.pfx` file or create a new self-signed one they are all kept in a list that is saved with the app settings so they come back after every restart.

The code only ever **added** to that list. Nothing removed an entry and the Sign with a Digital ID dialog. The only place the list is shown let's you pick an ID but not remove one.

## What changes for the user

- **Remove** sits next to **Configure New Digital ID** and works on the selected ID.
- It **asks first** to *Remove "Name" from this list? The file itself is not deleted.*, with **Remove** and **Cancel**.

- The removal is saved so the ID removed forever after a restart.
- If no IDs are left the dialog goes to **Configure a Digital ID** as it does when you have never added one.
- **Keychain (macOS) and Windows certificate store IDs** can't be removed here instead the button is greyed out for them. The OS manages by itself and PdfCraft lists them again each time you sign.

`crates/ui-egui/src/sign_ui.rs`
- New `PdfCraftApp::remove_digital_id(index)`. It refuses OS store IDs and indexes past the list, removes the entry and keeps the dialog's selection on the same ID (or the first usable one if the selected ID was removed).
- `SignDraft::confirm_remove` holds the ID waiting for confirmation. Clicking another row cancels the question.
- No change is needed in saving: `persist()` already saves whatever is in the list.

title: fix(audit): a rectangle drawn as an m/l path is a cover like re
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1510.

The cover walk in `crates/audit/src/cover.rs` only kept a pending rectangle for `re`; every `m`/`l`/`h` reset it, so the same black box drawn as a closed path was never seen as a cover. The pending `re` rectangle is now a small path state: a single `m`/`l` subpath has its corners mapped through the CTM as it is built, and on fill it counts when its four corners (a repeated start point is dropped) alternate horizontal and vertical edges in user space. It then goes through the same opacity and colour checks as `re`. title: M3: draw a GNOME-style title bar on Wayland (#553)
author: bmh129
body:
## Summary
Fixes #553. Part of #1001.

GNOME's Wayland compositor draws no window frames (it offers no `zxdg_decoration_manager_v1`), so winit drew its own fallback title bar. That bar ignores GNOME's theme, dark mode and button layout. PdfCraft now asks the compositor at launch (`apps/pdfcraft/src/decorations.rs`). Where the compositor draws no frames, PdfCraft turns winit's frame off and makes the tab strip the header bar, as GNOME's own apps do (`crates/ui-egui/src/window_controls.rs`):

- **Window buttons:** minimize, maximize/restore and close in Adwaita's style. They are round, with symbolic glyphs drawn in code, so no new assets. They follow the order and side given by `org.gnome.desktop.wm.preferences button-layout`, read through `gsettings`; Fedora's default `appmenu:close` shows only close. They're hidden in full screen.
- **Resizing:** zones along the edges, plus L-shaped corners, sit above the rest of the UI, so a press there resizes the window instead of reaching a scrollbar. A hairline outlines the window while it isn't maximized.
- **Preferences ▸ Use system title bar:** shown only where the app draws the frame. It gives the window back winit's frame at once, without a restart. It's named as in VectorCraft and PhotoCraft, but GNOME draws no title bars for apps, so on GNOME this is winit's basic frame; the tooltip says so. Saved as `system_title_bar`, and settable on the control channel as `system-title-bar`.
- **`PDFCRAFT_TITLEBAR=app|system`** overrides the detection (documented in `docs/development.md`).

Unchanged elsewhere:
- KDE, Sway, Hyprland, COSMIC and X11 offer server-side decorations, so they keep the frame their desktop draws.
- macOS and Windows are unchanged.

### Not done
- Right-clicking the header bar doesn't open GNOME's window menu (egui has no command for it).
- The window has no shadow or rounded corners.
- The resize zones lie just inside the window rather than outside it.

Two macOS quit bugs, both fixed through `craft-quit` from craft-libs (storytold/craft-libs#5 and #21, now merged; pinned to craft-libs `main` at `f58bc1a`).

**Part 2: ⌘Q quits without asking to save.** winit's default app menu sends Quit straight to `-[NSApplication terminate:]`, which skips `guard_quit`. `apps/pdfcraft` now calls `craft_quit::install_app_menu(&cc.egui_ctx, "PdfCraft")` from the app creator. title: fix(xfdf): preserve quoted empty CSV values
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
A one-column CSV file whose only value is a quoted empty string, such as `Name\r\n""\r\n` (what Python's `csv.writer` writes for an empty value in a one-column row), now clears the field. Before, `import_table` dropped every record whose single cell was empty, quoted or not, so this import returned `UnknownFormat`.

The CSV parser now records whether each record contained a quote. Unquoted blank lines, including the one a trailing line break leaves, are still skipped. A line holding only `""` now counts as a record wherever it appears, as RFC 4180 reads it, so `Name\n""\nGrace\n` clears the field instead of taking `Grace`. An unquoted empty value in a one-column file (`Name\n\n`) stays ambiguous and still reports `UnknownFormat`.

Tests in `crates/xfdf/src/tests.rs`:
- `quoted_empty_csv_value_clears_a_field` covers LF, CRLF, no final newline, a blank line before the value, and a later record after it. It fails on main with `UnknownFormat` and passes here.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-xfdf` passes (30 tests), and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps passed.

title: M3: scroll the view when drawing at an edge; take back a polygon's last point
author: philip-tam
body:
## What

Two fixes for drawing comments (Polygon, Cloud, Connected lines, and the other drawing tools):

1. **Edge scrolling.** While a drawing is in progress, the pointer in a 32 px band along any edge of the document view (or just past it) scrolls the view up, down, left or right, so a point beyond what is shown can be reached without leaving the tool. The speed grows with the square of the depth into the band. It only applies within one band of the view, so the pointer over a side panel never scrolls the page. `edge_scroll` is in `crates/ui-egui/src/autoscroll.rs`; `canvas.rs` adds its result to the existing scroll delta.
2. **Take back a point.** Backspace, Delete or Undo (Cmd/Ctrl+Z) removes the last point of a polygon, cloud or run of connected lines being drawn. Removing the only point cancels the drawing. Undo only does this while such a drawing is in progress (`CommentView::undo_point`, called first from `PdfCraftApp::undo`); otherwise it behaves as before.

## Tests

- New unit tests for the edge-scroll maths: all four directions, the middle and far-away pointers, non-finite input, speed rising toward and past the edge.
- New UI test `a_wrong_polygon_point_is_taken_back_with_backspace_or_undo` (Backspace, Undo, re-clicking, finishing, and cancelling by removing the only point).
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean, and `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui` passes.
- No automated test scrolls the real page while drawing; I tried it by hand in a packaged macOS build (Apple Silicon) and it works there. Not tried on Windows, Linux or the web.
- I did not run the full workspace tests for this change.

title: M14: Fix(nixos): discover installed UI fallback fonts on NixOS
author: tomasmark79

title: Keep annotations readable under reading colours (#1548)
author: edurbs
body:
Fixes #1548.

## What

With reading colours on a dark preset, every highlight annotation rendered as a solid dark bar and the text under it was invisible (contrast ≈ 1:1). After this PR, the marked-up words render in the highlight's own colour — yellow words on black, ≈ 19:1 contrast — matching the Acrobat model where Replace Document Colors recolours *document* text and line art but never the colours a comment was given.

## Why (two causes)

1. **Annotation paints were remapped as line art.** `ColorReplacement::map` sends luminance-light paints toward the background, so the yellow fill became near-black; Multiply then darkened the remapped-white words under it into invisibility.
2. **The page background sat outside the page transparency group.** A group isolates what it wraps, so a Multiply highlight blended only with the group's transparent backdrop and never with the background — even with the annotation colour left alone, the quad would stay one flat bar with the words lost in it.

## How

- **hayro patch 26:** the `/Annots` loop in `interpret_page` is bracketed by a new `begin_annotations`/`end_annotations` `Device` signal (default no-ops), and the renderer's reading-colours mapping leaves annotation paints alone while it is set. Covers both paths: `/AP` appearance streams and the no-`/AP` `/QuadPoints` fallback; sibling cases (a black annotation underline flipping bright, light annotation colours vanishing) are fixed by the same rule.
- **hayro patch 27:** the page background is painted *inside* the page transparency group, as the initial backdrop, so Multiply blends with it. White pages are unaffected — multiplying with white is the identity (all existing light-mode render tests pass unchanged).

Display only, as the setting itself: the document is not changed, print and export are unaffected.

## Testing

title: M2: draw non-embedded CJK CID fonts with an installed face
author: philip-tam
body:
## What

A CID font of an Adobe CJK collection (Adobe-Japan1, GB1, CNS1, Korea1) that a PDF does not embed drew nothing unless craft-fonts had a Japanese face. Text boxes written by other tools with a non-embedded CJK font (for example Kozuka Gothic from Acrobat, or SongtiTC from macOS Quartz) were blank in builds without craft-fonts, and Chinese or Korean text was blank even with it.

After the craft-fonts Japanese faces, the renderer now uses one face already installed on the machine, before hayro's Latin-only fallback. hayro already maps the CIDs of all four collections to Unicode (UCS-2 CMaps); only a face was missing.

## How

- New `crates/render/src/system_font.rs`, wired in `RenderConfig::settings` after `japanese_fallback`.
- The face is read at runtime from well-known OS paths and is never bundled or shipped (AGENTS.md §1.4). Noto CJK and Source Han are not candidates (§1.1). `PDFCRAFT_SYSTEM_FONTS=0` turns it off, as for the interface font; wasm32 does nothing.
- A file is only read if it is a regular file under 96 MB; a face must map a probe character of the script (物, 欢, 說, 한), so a Latin-only font is never chosen.
- In a collection holding several regions (PingFang SC / TC / HK), the face is chosen by region, then by weight (regular, or semibold/bold for bold text).
- Results are cached per script and weight.
- macOS: PingFang, Hiragino, STHeiti, Apple SD Gothic Neo. Windows: Microsoft YaHei / JhengHei, Yu Gothic, Meiryo, MS Gothic, SimSun, MingLiU, Malgun. Linux: WenQuanYi, Droid Sans Fallback, AR PL UMing, Nanum, Takao/IPA. The Windows and Linux lists are untested.

title: M4: Mirror PDF pages horizontally and vertically (#1534)
author: LabDennis
body:
PdfCraft can rotate pages, but cannot mirror a scanned sheet, drawing or other PDF page. This adds **Flip horizontal** and **Flip vertical** to Organize Pages, the Pages menu and the command palette. They act on the selected pages (or the current page), and the corresponding CLI/MCP tools can mirror selected pages or the whole document.

Fixes #1534.

The operation reflects content about the visible CropBox in the displayed orientation, including inherited quarter-turn rotations and nonzero box origins. It adds small transform streams around the original content; it does not rasterize, decompress or rewrite the existing streams. Annotation rectangles, drawing coordinates, popup rectangles and stored appearance streams move with the content. Shared appearances are copied before changing their matrices, while field values, link actions and unknown dictionary entries remain intact.

The core separates annotation ownership checks, per-page transforms, content wrapping and annotation traversal, with a single atomic edit boundary. Duplicate page selections are handled once. Invalid geometry and annotations shared across pages fail atomically. Mirroring requires content-modification permission; assembly-only permission is insufficient. Each action is one undo step, and the mirrored result survives incremental save and reopening. Applying the same reflection twice restores the original appearance.

Automation tools: `page_flip_horizontal` and `page_flip_vertical`, with `{doc, pages?}`; omitted pages means all pages. Their command IDs are `page.flip_horizontal` and `page.flip_vertical`. The feature guide documents selection, direction and permission behavior. Existing localized labels and icons are reused.

### Screenshot

Organize Pages after flipping the selected second page horizontally. Pages 1 and 3 remain unchanged; both flip controls are available beside the rotation controls.

title: M3: Wayland: stop retaining Ctrl zoom for pixel-only wheel input
author: tomasmark79
body:
Related to #991.

The vendored Wayland pointer handler decides whether scrolling is a finger gesture using only the presence of discrete steps. A wheel event with pixel deltas and `axis_source=wheel` therefore emits `Started`, followed by `Moved`. Wayland does not guarantee `axis_stop` for wheel, wheel-tilt or continuous sources, so egui can stay in its touch gesture indefinitely and retain Ctrl after it is released. Subsequent wheel input keeps zooming.

Use the reported axis source when choosing the phase. These sources emit `Moved`, following the same policy as discrete wheel steps, so egui uses the current modifiers. Explicit stop events, finger gestures (including their modifier retention for momentum), and unknown-source behavior retain their existing policy. Pixel deltas and scroll speed are unchanged.

The regression test compiles the production phase policy and drives a real egui context through Ctrl+wheel followed by wheel without Ctrl. It fails on the previous policy (zoom remains `1.1274968` instead of `1.0`) and passes with the fix. Additional tests cover wheel tilt, continuous sources, discrete wheels, finger momentum and unknown sources. The patch and its tests are recorded in `vendor/README.md`.

Wayland protocol reference: [wl_pointer.axis_source](https://wayland.freedesktop.org/docs/html/apa.html#protocol-spec-wl_pointer-event-axis_source).

- Merge upstream through `e88dd72` and resolve the roadmap conflicts.
- Share the Linux winit dev-dependency, pointer modules and vendor patch documentation with #1580; that branch includes this change and its combined workspace run passed (3,025 tests, 14 ignored), as did strict Clippy and the full wasm gate. Merge this PR before #1580.

title: Issue #1058: an update keeps the desktop shortcut only if it is still there
author: pauliusiv123-rgb
body:
Fixes #1058.

**Cause.** The ArtCraft Launcher installs and updates PdfCraft with `msiexec /i … /passive /norestart` and passes no properties, so `INSTALLDESKTOPSHORTCUT` always took its default of `1`. Every update put the desktop shortcut back, even for users who had deleted it, and deleting it is the only way a launcher user can say no.

**Fix** (`packaging/windows/pdfcraft.wxs`). `INSTALLDESKTOPSHORTCUT` no longer has a static default. Instead:
- AppSearch looks for `PdfCraft.lnk` on the all-users desktop. This runs before the old version is removed.
- A `SetProperty` after AppSearch sets the property to `1` for a first install. For an update it does so only if the shortcut is still there.
- A value given on the command line wins, as before.

The result for each case:

| Case | Desktop shortcut |
|---|---|
| First install (full UI or launcher) | Created; the checkbox starts ticked, as before |
| `INSTALLDESKTOPSHORTCUT=0` | Not created |
| Update, shortcut still on the desktop | Kept |
| Update, shortcut deleted (or unticked at install) | Not added back |

This needs no new registry state, and it works for updates from 0.7.1 and earlier, which never recorded a choice. The ArtCraft Launcher's own installer takes the same approach to its shortcut, with a remembered choice. That wouldn't help here, because launcher users never make a choice the MSI could record.

**Tests** (`packaging/windows/test-msi.ps1`):
- `INSTALLDESKTOPSHORTCUT` has no `Property` row.
- The SetProperty action comes after AppSearch in both sequences.
- Windows Installer's evaluator checks its condition for five cases: first install, first install with `=0`, update with the shortcut, update without it, and update with `=0`.

The MSI builds with WiX, `test-msi.ps1` passes, and the ARM64 install and uninstall smoke test passes. That smoke test doesn't check desktop shortcuts for PdfCraft. Fork run: https://github.com/pauliusiv123-rgb/printcraft/actions/runs/38301587407

title: Name the failing option and page count when a chained edit page is out of range (#1550)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1550.

The wrong page number in the report wasn't caused by the chaining. `OrganizeError::NoSuchPage` holds a 0-based index, but its message printed that index as is. So `--move 5:1` on a document with 4 pages (index 4) said "page 4 does not exist". The same thing happens without chaining: `--rotate 9:90` on a 5-page file said "page 8".

**Changes**

- **The message counts from 1.** `NoSuchPage` in `pdfcraft-organize` now prints `page {index + 1} does not exist`. This fixes every caller that shows the error, including the CLI, the app and automation. `pdfcraft-edit` and `pdfcraft-annot` had the same 0-based message on their `NoSuchPage` variants, and every constructor there also passes a 0-based index, so they get the same fix.
- **`edit` names the option and the current page count**, as the issue suggests. Before each operation, `pdfcraft-cli edit` checks the `--rotate`/`--delete`/`--move` pages against the page count left by the earlier options. The error looks like `--move: page 5 does not exist; after the earlier options the document has 4 pages`. This follows the existing per-edit check for `--move` targets and `--insert-blank` positions (#1330).
- **`--help`** now says that the options run in order and that page numbers refer to the document after the earlier options.

**Tests**

- `apps/pdfcraft-cli/tests/edit.rs`: `a_page_past_the_end_after_earlier_edits_names_that_option` grows a 1-page file to 3 pages, deletes page 3, then asks for `--move 3:1`. It checks that the error names `--move`, page 3 and the 2 pages that are left, and that no output file is written.

title: M3: enable native touchpad pinch zoom on Wayland
author: tomasmark79
body:
Related to #1095; implements the missing Wayland input path.

This branch includes #1569 to reconcile the shared Wayland pointer module, Linux winit test dependency and vendor documentation. Merge #1569 first; this PR then contains the remaining pinch change. Both policies are validated together against upstream `e88dd72`.

The PDF viewer already handles egui zoom events, and #1148 added a synthetic viewer test. title: Print: 4 x 6 in label paper and a Label layout for shipping labels
author: Ace40063
body:
## Problem

Shipping labels (eBay, carriers) could not be printed properly on a 4 x 6 in thermal label printer (tested with a VEVOR Y486, CUPS on macOS):

- the paper list had no 4 x 6 in size;
- the paper chosen in the dialog was never sent to CUPS, so the queue's default size was used whatever the PDF was laid out on;
- labels laid out sideways on a Letter/A4 sheet came out small, rotated or cut.

## Changes

- **Paper**: `PAPERS` gains `4 x 6 in label (101.6 x 152.4 mm)` (288 x 432 pt).
- **Spooler**: `print::cups_media()` maps the chosen paper to a CUPS media name and the job passes it as `-o media=` (Letter, Legal, Tabloid, A3, A4, A5, and `w288h432` for the label). Papers without a common PPD name send nothing, as before.

  - a page that is sideways relative to the sheet is turned a quarter turn in the direction that makes its text upright: `print::text_reads_up` reads the text (`Tm`) and `cm` matrices, following form XObjects;
  - the crop is fitted uniformly with an 8 pt margin (several 4 x 6 drivers feed 100 x 150 mm, slightly short of 288 x 432 pt);
  - content stays vector, so barcodes stay sharp and undistorted; "Turn upside down (180°)" flips it; one label per sheet.
- Choosing the label paper selects the Label layout, and the Label tab selects the label paper.
- New strings translated in every bundled catalog.

## Testing

- New unit tests: label geometry (crop kept as clip, quarter turns in both directions and the 180° flip, uniform scale/no stretching, margins, whole page when there is no crop), `cups_media`, text direction.

title: M2: average images shrunk more than 2:1 even without /Interpolate
author: philip-tam
body:
## What

A page that is one big image without `/Interpolate` (the usual scan of text) showed broken thin strokes at screen size: a Chinese "自" read as "白", "土" as "上", boxed characters opened up. The image was shrunk by picking single source pixels (the PDF default when `/Interpolate` is absent), which drops strokes thinner than the step between picked pixels. Acrobat, pdfium and poppler average the pixels.

## Why only beyond 2:1

#624 made non-interpolated images use nearest-neighbour so screenshots and rasterized text stay crisp, and tests such as `non_interpolated_images_are_not_smoothed_when_minified` pin that at 2:1. Nearest is fine there. Beyond 2:1 it loses information, and a scan at 300 dpi shown at screen size is usually 2.5:1 to 6:1.

## Change (`vendor/hayro/src/renderer.rs`, `draw_image`)

- An image shrunk by more than 2:1 (`MIN_NEAREST_SCALE = 0.5` device pixels per source pixel on either axis) is resampled by the interpolating resampler (Catmull-Rom with a kernel that grows on downscaling) and gets the whole-pixel snapping from #1377, even without `/Interpolate`.
- Up to 2:1 nothing changes.
- A source the resampler cannot take (over 2^20 pixels wide, or over its plan budget) keeps the old nearest path, so `wide_non_interpolated_sources_draw_after_shrinking` still holds.
- The image/soft-mask pairing check compares the PDF's own `/Interpolate` flags, not the new decision, so a soft-masked image does not re-enter `draw_image_with_alpha_mask` forever (a first version of this change overflowed the stack in `image_resampling_wide_transparent_sources_still_shrink`).

## Tests

- New `raster::tests::non_interpolated_images_shrunk_more_than_two_to_one_are_averaged`: 1-pixel stripes drawn 3:1 are mid-grey (they alternate black and white when picked); the same stripes at exactly 2:1 are still picked.

title: XFA: a script's time starts when its context is ready, and a value reaches every field bound to its data node
author: ysrdevs
body:
## XFA: a script's time starts when its context is ready, and a value reaches every field bound to its data node

The two follow-ups asked for in #1355.

### Script time

The session's worker now sends a `Started` reply once the engine is ready for the script it was sent (its JavaScript context built; FormCalc has nothing to build and says so at once), and the script's time limit counts from then, with the engine's start limit (10 s) covering the phase before it. This is what the one-shot path (`run_within_limits`) always did; the session had lost it, so a context's build on a busy machine was charged to the script.

### Shared data nodes

A field inside an `area` and a field of the same name outside it bind to one data node, since areas are left out of data paths. The in-place refresh of the live form (`pdfcraft_xfa::refresh_value`) now follows the data path through the tree (through areas and unnamed containers, which have no data segment, so the walk costs the depth, not the form) and gives every field bound to the node the value the tree builder would, each computed by its own template field (saved values, template default); an exclusion group bound there makes it fall back to a rebuild, as a radio button already did. The engine's value setter keeps an index of widgets by data node (built with its SOM map, dropped on relayout) and gives every widget bound to the node the value, each by its own kind (a check box by its on state, a list box by lines), including when the field the script set has no widget of its own (hidden); the data is written when the node's text differs, whether or not the first widget already held it.

The adversarial review of the first cut found the naive version of this (a scan of all widgets per value, a walk of the whole tree) quadratic: a click setting 1000 totals in a 3000-widget form took 5.4 s against 0.4 s on main. With the index and the pruned walk the same click is linear again (300 values in a 300-row form: 52 ms in a debug build)…

title: fix(sign, packaging): sign with keys in legacy CryptoAPI providers; test-msi under Windows PowerShell 5.1
author: simscorpbs
body:
## What this fixes

### 1. Certificates whose key is in a legacy CryptoAPI provider can't sign (Windows)

Certificates whose private key lives in a legacy CryptoAPI provider (a CSP) are listed in
*Sign with a Digital ID* but disabled with:

> its private key's algorithm couldn't be read: Unsupported…

This hits Brazilian ICP-Brasil A3 certificates that register only a CSP. Example: Certisign's
desktopID cloud certificates, whose provider is "desktopID Cryptographic Provider"
(`PROV_RSA_AES`, `C:\Windows\System32\desktopID_Provider.DLL`), with no CNG KSP and no PKCS #11
module on Windows.

**Cause.** `windows.rs` opens every key through CNG (`CryptAcquireCertificatePrivateKey` with
`CRYPT_ACQUIRE_ONLY_NCRYPT_KEY_FLAG`, then `NCryptGetProperty`/`NCryptSignHash`). A CSP key has no
NCrypt handle, so reading its algorithm fails.

**Fix.**
- Listing reads the certificate's key provider info (`CERT_KEY_PROV_INFO_PROP_ID`). A provider type
  other than 0 means a legacy CSP. Such an RSA certificate counts as usable *without opening the key*,
  because a cloud provider would otherwise ask for approval on every listing.
- Signing a CSP key uses `CryptAcquireCertificatePrivateKey` with `CRYPT_ACQUIRE_ALLOW_NCRYPT_KEY_FLAG`
  (not silent, so the provider can show its own authorization). Then `CryptCreateHash` +
  `CryptSetHashParam(HP_HASHVAL)` + `CryptSignHashW`. The signature is byte-reversed, because CryptoAPI
  is little-endian. PKCS #1 v1.5 only: CryptoAPI has no PSS.
- If the acquired key turns out to be CNG (`CERT_NCRYPT_KEY_SPEC`), the existing CNG path signs it.
- The key is acquired and released per signature, so each signature can ask for authorization again.
- CNG certificates are unchanged.

**`unsafe`.** AGENTS.md forbids `unsafe` and asks for a maintained safe wrapper. None exists for
legacy CryptoAPI signing, as far as I could find. So the FFI is isolated in one small new crate,
`crates/wincapi` (layer 0, standalone, Windows-only). It declares the exception in it…

title: feat(sign): sign with PKCS #11 devices (smart cards, USB tokens, cloud certificates)
author: simscorpbs
body:
## What this adds

Signing with a Digital ID on a **PKCS #11 device**: smart cards, USB tokens, and cloud
certificates whose vendor ships a PKCS #11 module. Examples: Certisign desktopID, Soluti birdID,
Serpro NeoID. The private key never leaves the device; signing goes through `C_Sign`.

This is how signing works for lawyers and companies in Brazil, where ICP-Brasil A3 certificates
(OAB, e-CPF, e-CNPJ) live on tokens or in the cloud. Until now PdfCraft could only reach them when the
OS exposed them (Keychain/CryptoTokenKit, Windows store). Most tokens and every cloud certificate on
macOS and Linux are reachable only through their vendor's PKCS #11 library.

### Finding devices

`crates/sign/src/pkcs11.rs` looks for the libraries device vendors install in their usual places on
macOS, Windows and Linux. The list follows what Brazilian court signers such as PJeOffice search,
plus desktopID for Apple Silicon, YubiKey (ykcs11) and OpenSC.
- Only existing files are loaded, each once. A library linked under two names counts once.
- A library that doesn't load (another architecture, a broken install) is skipped and logged.
- 32-bit Windows libraries are not listed.
- `PDFCRAFT_PKCS11_MODULES` (a path list) replaces the search, for testing.

### In the UI

- *Configure a Digital ID for Signing* gets a third option: **Use a Digital ID from a device
  (smart card, USB token or cloud certificate)**, as in Acrobat. The library field is optional: empty
  re-reads the devices, and a chosen library (*Browse…*) is checked, kept in the settings
  (`pkcs11_modules`) and read from then on. A library that isn't PKCS #11 is refused with the reason.
- Device certificates appear in *Sign with a Digital ID* with the device's label
  ("desktopID · Issued by …").
- A device with a PIN takes it in the password field, labelled **PIN**. A device with a protected
  authentication path (a PIN pad, or a cloud certificate approved on the phone) takes none. PdfCraft
  logs in to it in the background…

title: Detect rectangular form fields drawn with closed line paths
author: FredApps
body:
Refs #294.

A synthetic regression reproduces different detection geometry for equivalent rectangle encodings: `50 100 120 40 re S` produces a rectangle, while the same outline written with `m/l/h` produces only its top and bottom rules. Treating those edges as rules gives the default rule-field sizing instead of the printed rectangle's height. This change makes both encodings detect one 38-point field inside the 40-point outline, including through the real Detect fields command and save/reopen.

This is a partial fix. The reporter's PDF was unavailable, so the synthetic case demonstrates a cause consistent with the report, not proof of that file's exact cause. Border/default-style concerns and broader detection accuracy remain out of scope. The broader issue remains open.

The shape pass tracks straight subpaths until painting and recognizes axis-aligned four-edge rectangles with explicit closepath, close-and-stroke, repeated endpoints, or implicit fill closure. Stroke closure applies to the last subpath; fill closure applies to all. Rectangle edges do not become extra rule fields, while unrelated horizontal rules remain available. Curves, diagonals, open stroked outlines, and continued complex paths are not promoted to rectangles. The existing CTM is applied to points; controls cover scaling, restored graphics state, and 90-degree rotation. Recorded rectangle corners are bounded to four corners plus a repeated endpoint, and non-finite coordinates are rejected.

Validation on the committed tree:
- 67 forms tests passed, including equivalent encodings, closure/paint variants, negative controls, mixed subpaths, clip-only discard, and CTM handling.

title: M13: Run conversion, OCR and optimization over folder trees
author: LabDennis
body:
The CLI could run individual tools or selected-file actions, but could not apply a conversion/OCR/compression recipe to a folder tree. This adds `pdfcraft-cli batch` and the shared `doc_batch` CLI/MCP tool.

```sh
pdfcraft-cli batch scans --root . --recursive --steps convert,ocr,optimize --out-dir processed
```

The runner discovers inputs before writing, preserves paths relative to each selected folder, deduplicates overlapping selections and processes one file at a time in an isolated engine session. It reuses the existing importers, OCR settings and optimizer. `--ppi` and `--quality` configure the Reduce File Size image settings; a larger optimization candidate retains the entering bytes.

Outputs are published through `NamedTempFile::persist_noclobber`, with numbered names on collisions, including concurrent writers. Sources and caller documents stay unchanged. Each file is published only after its complete recipe succeeds. Errors are reported per file; `--stop-on-error` is optional. The CLI prints the JSON report and exits nonzero on partial failure; MCP retains structured results and sets `isError`.

Discovery skips links/reparse points, special files and nested output folders. Root confinement is checked before discovery and before processing. Traversal is limited to 1,000 selected roots, 10,000 entries and 64 levels; individual inputs are limited to 512 MiB. The new code lives in two small modules rather than expanding the existing command dispatchers. The existing OCR argument parser is shared.

See `docs/cli-batch.md` for examples and boundaries. This is a one-shot command; it adds no watcher, service, scheduler or GUI workflow and is independent of the hot-folder work in #1063. Conversion uses the engine's supported extensions, so comic archives become available when #1587 lands without duplicating its importer here. The batch parity entry remains partial because arbitrary Action Wizard recipes, GUI folder selection and resuming are not implemented.

title: feat(ui): interface font and text rendering options (Preferences ▸ Appearance)
author: simscorpbs
body:
## What this adds

Two options in **Preferences ▸ Appearance**, both defaulting to today's look:

- **Interface font:**
  - *Standard (Inter)*: as now.
  - *System font*: read from the installed fonts, never embedded.
    - macOS: SF Pro (`SFNS.ttf`, at AppKit's 400/510/590 weights) and SF Mono.
    - Windows: Segoe UI Variable and Cascadia Mono (Consolas if missing).
  - *Font file* (.ttf, .otf, .ttc): a variable file gives its regular, medium and semibold
    weights.
  - The chosen faces go *in front of* the embedded ones, which stay as the fallback. A file that
    can't be read changes nothing.
- **Text rendering:**
  - *Standard*: as now.
  - *Like macOS (fuller strokes, sub-pixel placement)*: measured against AppKit text at 2x.
    - Glyph outlines grow 0.15 px, CoreText's font smoothing.
    - Glyphs sit at quarter-pixel offsets.
    - Light-theme coverage uses gamma 0.9.
    - With SF Pro, ink and covered area land within 98–101% of AppKit's.

Fonts are rebuilt when either option changes; no restart.

### epaint patch (vendored)

System fonts like SF Pro need two things egui doesn't do yet:
- the optical size following the point size (variable `opsz`);
- Apple's `trak` tracking.

Without them, SF Pro reads looser and lighter than in native apps. Both are proposed upstream as
**emilk/egui#8707**. Until it lands, `vendor/epaint` (0.36.2) carries them, plus PdfCraft's own
glyph dilation for *Like macOS*. Each patch is marked `PdfCraft patch:` and listed in
`vendor/README.md`, as for the other vendored crates.

In Acrobat, Edit on a scanned page first converts it ("Converting scanned page to Editable Text and Images"), so its words can be edited. title: Fix Intel Mac crash: probe Metal shader language version support
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary

Fixes crashes on Intel Macs where all ArtCraft apps fail to launch with `Metal: error: invalid value 'metal3.2' in '-std=metal3.2'`.

The wgpu Metal backend was choosing MSL version purely from OS version, but legacy Intel GPUs have older Metal compilers that reject newer MSL versions.

## Solution

Vendors wgpu-hal 30.0.1 with the patch from gfx-rs/wgpu#10592:
- Probes the Metal compiler at adapter creation by compiling a test kernel
- Steps down from OS-selected version until compiler accepts it
- Modern Macs: tries Metal 3.2 → succeeds immediately
- Legacy Intel Macs: tries 3.2 → 3.1 → ... → 2.4/2.3 until one works

## Issues Fixed

Fixes storytold/photocraft#1859
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2126  
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2190

## Testing

- ✅ Compiles on macOS
- ✅ Passes clippy
- ⚠️ Untested on real Intel Mac hardware (awaiting community testing)

## Notes

The vendored wgpu-hal will be removed once upstream releases the fix and ArtCraft can bump to that version.

---
— sent on behalf of @mjohnson7cd by Claude Code

title: feat(sign): sign with ICP-Brasil cloud certificates (PSC API)
author: simscorpbs
body:
## What this adds

Signing with a **cloud certificate** through the API that Brazil's ICP-Brasil defines for its
cloud signature providers (PSC), DOC-ICP-17.01. BirdID, VIDaaS, NeoID, SafeID and the other
accredited providers implement the same endpoints, so one client reaches all of them. The key never
leaves the provider: PdfCraft sends the digest and gets back the raw signature.

### Protocol (`crates/sign/src/psc.rs`)

- OAuth 2.0 authorization code with PKCE (S256, RFC 7636), scope `signature_session`.
- `oauth/token` for the session, `oauth/certificate-discovery` for the certificates (RSA only,
  as the CMS builder signs with RSA), `oauth/signature` with `signature_format: RAW`.
- `CloudKey` implements `ExternalKey`, so the existing CMS/PAdES path signs with it unchanged.
- HTTP goes through a small `Transport` trait. The app implements it with `ureq` and the OS roots it
  already uses for updates (`apps/pdfcraft/src/psc_http.rs`); the crate stays free of networking.

### Sign-in (`crates/ui-egui/src/cloud_sign.rs`)

- A loopback redirect (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` or `localhost`), bound before the browser
  opens. Other redirect URIs are refused with the reason.
- The `state` is checked, the wait ends after 5 minutes, and the browser gets a plain
  "you can close this page".
- Runs on a thread; the UI polls it and repaints when it finishes.

### Providers and credentials

Each provider issues a client ID and secret to the **app**, when the app is registered with it (as
gov.br is with each of them); the holder never sees them and only signs in on the provider's page
with CPF, PIN and one-time code. So:

- `psc::KNOWN` lists the providers whose API base is known. It starts with Certisign
  (`https://remoteidcertisign.com.br/api/v0/`); others are one line each once their address is
  confirmed.
- The desktop app reads each provider's credentials at build time
  (`PDFCRAFT_PSC_<NAME>_CLIENT_ID` and `PDFCRAFT_PSC_<NAME>_CLIENT_SECRET`, e.g. from CI secret…

title: Windows: Harden single-instance IPC security
author: mjshfrvstj-sys
body:
## Summary

Strengthen the Windows AF_UNIX document handoff merged in #715 while retaining its existing socket architecture, startup election, document-opening route and separate-window fallback.

## Motivation

This follows [echelon's invitation to harden the merged socket implementation in the closing feedback on #616](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/616#issuecomment-6096621666). The changes address the requested security improvements while retaining the architecture and compatibility behavior established by #715. In particular, this contribution does not reintroduce named pipes, fatal handoff dialogs, altered secondary-launch behavior, or additional dependency packages.

Refs #616, #715, #602, #282 and #317. These references do not close the broader cross-platform or tab-management requests.

## Security improvements

- Bind each exchange to fresh primary/client nonces inside Windows `LOCAL=user` protected envelopes. Document paths remain sealed, the primary verifies its challenge before admitting a batch, and the client verifies both nonces in the acknowledgment. No reusable secret file is introduced.
- Reject malformed, truncated and oversized length-prefixed frames before unbounded allocation. Enforce versioned document-only schemas, absolute/NUL-free paths, 256 paths per batch, 32 KiB per path and a 1 MiB plaintext limit.
- Bound admission to four receivers and eight active/waiting connections, with at most 16 pending batches, 1,024 paths and 4 MiB of path data. Queue saturation rejects the entire batch before acknowledgment.
- Apply total exchange deadlines to queue wait, nonblocking IO and async crypto waits, so trickled data cannot refresh them. Shutdown signals and joins the fixed workers.
- Derive profile/session routing from Windows known-folder and token APIs instead of environment variables. Check local parents and lock files for reparse points; refuse unlocked election, preserve unrelated regular files, and remove stale sockets only after …
